.“작품은 어디에 있는가? 벽에 있는가? 바닥에 있는가? 공간 안에 있는.en: .“Where is the work? Is it on the wall? On the floor? In space? Or am I the work?” The exhibition “Line Drawing a Cone 2.0” focuses on Anthony McCall’s Solid Light work and highlights his world of work that crosses the boundaries of film, sculpture, and installation. A moving line of light slowly crosses space, creating a cone-like shape, and the process appears as an event created in time rather than as a fixed result. He began his work in the early 1970s through a film project called ‘Expanded Cinema’, and in 1973 he presented ‘Line Drawing a Cone’, a work using cigarette smoke and a 16mm projector. A single line drawing projected on the wall formed a huge cone shape in space, but it was difficult to continue this work due to the stereotypes and technical limitations of the time. He stopped working for about 20 years, and in the early 2000s, he entered another turning point by converting his film work to digital files. Technological shifts affected not only the form of the work but also its philosophical depth. The white noise produced by the film projector has disappeared, allowing visitors to focus more on their bodies, senses, and inner self. Simple line animation has evolved into rhythmic drawing lines, and the fog filled with cigarette smoke has been replaced with a haze machine, revealing a clearer light structure. The most notable change in his work since the 2000s is that the viewer's physical intervention is more actively required. The viewer no longer stays in front of the screen, but is guided into the cone-shaped structure formed by light. The body facing the work appears cut or divided by the light. The basic act of the viewer existing, moving, and moving within the space becomes a part of the work. Here, light is no longer an object to look at, but acts as an experience that the body perceives as it passes through it. 〈Line Drawing a Cone 2.0〉 is not an exhibition that presents a completed shape. The exhibition allows you to encounter the process of drawing light, place your body within it, and directly experience the forms that are created and disappear in time. At this time, the work is not formed on the screen, but within the viewer's body, senses, and the space of that moment. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
.“작품은 어디에 있는가? 벽에 있는가? 바닥에 있는가? 공간 안에 있는.zh: “作品在哪里？是在墙上吗？在地板上？在太空中？还是我就是作品？”展览“Line Drawing a Cone 2.0”重点展示了安东尼·麦考尔的《Solid Light》作品，并突出了他跨越电影、雕塑和装置界限的作品世界。一条移动的光线缓慢地穿过空间，形成一个圆锥体的形状，这个过程看起来像是一个及时发生的事件，而不是一个固定的结果。他于 20 世纪 70 年代初通过一个名为“扩展电影”的电影项目开始了自己的工作，并于 1973 年推出了“画圆锥线”，这是一部使用香烟烟雾和 16 毫米投影仪的作品。投影在墙上的单幅线条画在空间中形成了一个巨大的圆锥体形状，但由于当时的刻板印象和技术限制，这项工作很难继续下去。他停止工作了大约20年，2000年代初，他将电影作品转换为数字文件，进入了另一个转折点。技术变革不仅影响作品的形式，还影响其哲学深度。电影放映机产生的白噪音消失了，让参观者能够更加关注自己的身体、感官和内在自我。简单的线条动画演变为有节奏的画线，充满香烟烟雾的雾气被烟雾机取代，显露出更清晰的光结构。自2000年代以来，他的作品最显着的变化是更加积极地需要观众的身体干预。观看者不再停留在屏幕前，而是被引导到由光形成的锥形结构中。面向作品的身体似乎被光线切割或分割。观看者在空间中存在、移动、移动的基本行为成为作品的一部分。在这里，光不再是一个可供观看的物体，而是一种身体穿过它时所感知的体验。 《Line Drawing a Cone 2.0》并不是一个呈现完整形状的展览。展览让你体验绘制光的过程，将你的身体置于其中，直接体验在时间中产生和消失的形式。此时，作品不再是在屏幕上形成的，而是在观看者的身体、感官和那一刻的空间中形成的。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

제19회 베니스비엔날레 국제건축전 한국관 전시는 건립 30년을 맞이한 한.en: The Korean Pavilion exhibition at the 19th Venice Biennale International Architecture Exhibition explores the architecture of the Korean Pavilion, which has celebrated its 30th anniversary. The meaning of the pavilion, which has been used in numerous exhibitions so far, is reexamined from the perspective of ‘home’. This exhibition explores the future of the Korean Pavilion by highlighting its founding and past. The exhibition consists of research and visuals that trigger awareness of these issues by viewing the pavilion not as a neutral exhibition site but as an organic living thing with multi-layered meaning. ‘Thick, Thick, Thick’, taken from a traditional Korean children’s song, is a metaphorical framework for explaining these contents. ‘Thick, Thick’ is a house-building song sung while playing with dirt, reminiscent of Grotto, the primitive form of poly. The toad, the hidden speaker of the exhibition, symbolizes change and regeneration and evokes the old common legacies of Giardini Park, such as trees, land, sky, and sea. The homecoming exhibition held at the Arko Art Museum in Seoul was newly organized under different conditions from those in Venice. The first floor exhibition consists of materials related to the Korean pavilion's architecture and exhibition history and critically edited works, and serves as a public forum where related programs are held. The second floor exhibition examines how participating artists interpreted the conditions of the Korean pavilion and expanded it from a post-national perspective. The site-specific installation works shown in Venice are reorganized in a way that reveals the process and strategy during the return exhibition, and the audience experiences the exhibition along various paths of interpretation and practice. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
제19회 베니스비엔날레 국제건축전 한국관 전시는 건립 30년을 맞이한 한.zh: 第十九届威尼斯国际建筑双年展韩国馆展览探讨了庆祝成立 30 周年的韩国馆的建筑。迄今为止在众多展览中使用过的展馆的意义被从“家”的角度重新审视。本次展览通过强调韩国馆的成立和过去来探讨韩国馆的未来。该展览由研究和视觉效果组成，通过将展馆视为具有多层次意义的有机生物，而不是一个中立的展览场地，引发人们对这些问题的认识。 “厚厚厚”取自一首韩国传统儿歌，是解释这些内容的隐喻框架。 《Thick, Thick》是一首在玩土时唱的建造房屋的歌曲，让人想起石窟（Grotto），即聚乙烯的原始形式。蟾蜍是展览中隐藏的发言人，象征着变化和再生，让人想起贾迪尼公园古老的共同遗产，如树木、土地、天空和海洋。首尔Arko美术馆举办的归乡展是在与威尼斯不同条件下新举办的。一楼展览由与韩国馆建筑和展览历史相关的材料以及经过严格编辑的作品组成，并作为举办相关活动的公共论坛。二楼的展览探讨了参展艺术家如何解读韩国馆的状况，并从后国家的角度对其进行扩展。威尼斯展出的场域装置作品以揭示回归展览的过程和策略的方式进行重组，观众沿着不同的阐释和实践路径体验展览。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

제주의 대표 건축가이자 제주 건축문화의 형성과 발전에 지속적으로 이바지해.en: This is an opportunity to comprehensively highlight the architectural philosophy and major works of Kim Seok-yoon, Jeju's representative architect and architect who has continuously contributed to the formation and development of Jeju's architectural culture. It was planned to systematically understand the role that Kim Seok-yoon's work played in the formation and development of Jeju's modern architecture within Jeju's natural, social, and cultural conditions. This exhibition, jointly hosted and organized by the Jeju Museum of Art and the Jeju Architect Association of the Korean Institute of Architects, is held at the Jeju Museum of Contemporary Art, featuring the representative work of Kim Seok-yoon, winner of the Korea Institute of Architects Award in 2009. In that it reflects on the world of architecture in a space where the architect's thoughts are embodied, the exhibition also has symbolism and place that organically combines the content and location of the exhibition. 김창열미술관은 개관 10주년을 맞아 지난 10년간의 전시 역사를 되짚는.en: To celebrate its 10th anniversary, the Kim Chang-yeol Museum of Art has prepared an online exhibition that looks back on the history of exhibitions over the past 10 years. Among the 239 works owned by the museum, this exhibition introduces the 10 works that have been most frequently displayed and treated as important by curators. These works are the results that symbolically show the exhibition planning and research direction of the Kim Chang-yeol Museum of Art over the past 10 years. Through the repeatedly selected and illuminated works, we can naturally see what aesthetic values ​​the museum has placed at the center of Kim Tschang-yeol's art. Over the course of 10 years, these works have been seen by visitors at least 6 times and up to 9 times, establishing themselves as representative works of the museum. This online exhibition seeks to provide an opportunity to look back on the memories of exhibitions accumulated over the past 10 years and at the same time reflect on the essence and sustainability of Kim Tschang-yeol's art. 김창열미술관은 개관 10주년을 맞아 지난 10년간의 전시 역사를 되짚는.zh: 为庆祝建馆十周年，金昌烈美术馆准备了线上展览，回顾过去十年的展览历史。在该馆馆藏的239件作品中，本次展览介绍了展出次数最多且被策展人重视的10件作品。这些作品象征性地展现了金昌烈美术馆近10年来的展览策划和研究方向的成果。通过反复挑选和照亮的作品，我们自然可以看出博物馆将什么美学价值置于金昌烈艺术的中心。 10年来，这些作品被参观者参观了至少6次，最多9次，成为博物馆的代表作品。此次线上展览旨在提供一个机会，回顾过去十年积累的展览记忆，同时反思金昌烈艺术的本质和可持续性。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

국립중앙박물관(관장 유홍준)은 2026년 2월 12일(목)부터 상설전시실.en: The National Museum of Korea (Director Yoo Hong-jun) will be displaying the entire 22 volumes of 《Daedongyeojido (大東輿地圖)》 by Gosanja Kim Jeong-ho (1804?~1866?) Kim Jeong-ho (1804?~1866?) at the ‘Road of History’ on the first floor of the permanent exhibition hall from February 12, 2026 (Thursday). Exhibit. This exhibition is a special opportunity to view the entire Daedongyeojido, produced by Kim Jeong-ho in 1861 (the 12th year of King Cheoljong’s reign) at a glance. 3.8m wide, 6.7m tall... Meet the entire map of the overwhelming scale of ‘Daedongyeojido’ Daedongyeojido is a fold-and-fold map that divides Korea into 22 layers from north to south, with maps for each layer in one book. When all 22 volumes are connected, it becomes a large national map measuring about 6.7m long and 3.8m wide. The National Museum of Korea printed high-definition data from its collection of Daedongyeojido (Shinsu 19997) on traditional Korean paper, allowing visitors to appreciate its grand scale and detailed expressions at a glance. Through this, it is expected that people will be able to vividly experience the size and structure of the country as understood by people in the late Joseon Dynasty. Delicate mountain streams and streams, a road network marked every 10 ri... Daedongyeojido, created by Kim Jeong-ho, is considered the definitive map of the Joseon Dynasty and is a compilation of research results on Korea's old map production tradition. You can understand the pulse of the country through the accurately and detailed mountain ranges and watercourses, and dots are added every 10 ri on the roads to help you estimate the actual distance, adding convenience. In addition, various information about the society at the time, including administrative and defense information, economy, and transportation, was expressed in symbols. In particular, it is characteristic that a separate map table corresponding to the legend of a modern map was created so that users can easily and quickly understand a lot of geographical information. The tradition of our old maps and the achievements of Kim Jeong-ho The fact that Korea had an excellent map-making tradition can also be seen through <Honil Gangni Yeokdae National Road Map> produced in 1402 (the 2nd year of King Taejong's reign). <Donggukdaejido (東國大地圖)> produced by Jeong Sang-gi (1678-1752) during the reign of King Yeongjo using the scale of Baeknicheok, and Shin Gyeong-jun (1712-1781) produced it. 《Donggukyeojido》, etc. became the basis for the production of 《Daedongyeojido》. Prior to the production of 《Daedongyeojido》, Kim Jeong-ho compiled manuscript national maps such as 《Cheonggudo Map》 and 《Dongyeodo Dongyeodo》 and geographical books such as 『Daedongjiji』. 《Daedongyeojido》 was completed by compiling these map-making traditions. In particular, a feature of Daedongyeojido is that it was printed with woodblocks so that more people could easily carry and use the map. Yoo Hong-jun, director of the National Museum of Korea, said, “This exhibition will be a valuable opportunity to directly experience the great achievements of Kim Jeong-ho and the beauty of our country by encountering the Daedongyeojido, which was previously only available in book form, as a huge map.” He added, “I hope that you will feel pride in the excellence of our ancient maps through the Daedongyeojido, which contains the essence of science and art from the Joseon Dynasty.” The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
국립중앙박물관(관장 유홍준)은 2026년 2월 12일(목)부터 상설전시실.zh: 国立中央博物馆（柳洪俊馆长）将于2026年2月12日（星期四）起在常设展览馆一楼“历史之路”展示高三子金正浩（1804？~1866？）金正浩（1804？~1866？）的《大东地图》全22卷。展览。此次展览是一次可以一览金正浩于1861年（哲宗12年）制作的大同历志图整体的特别机会。宽3.8m，高6.7m……来认识一下《大同地图》压倒性规模的全图 大同地图是一张折叠式地图，将韩国从北到南分为22层，每一层的地图都在一本书里。将22卷全部连接起来，就成为一张长约6.7m、宽约3.8m的大型国家地图。韩国国家博物馆将其收藏的《大同历志图》（Shinsu 19997）的高清数据打印在传统的韩国纸上，让参观者一目了然地欣赏到其宏大的规模和细致的表达。通过此活动，人们将能够生动地体验到朝鲜后期人们所理解的国家的规模和结构。精致的山涧溪流、每十里就有一个道路网……金正浩创作的《大同地图》被认为是朝鲜王朝的权威地图，是韩国旧地图制作传统研究成果的汇编。通过准确细致的山脉和水道，您可以了解国家的脉搏，道路上每10里添加一个点，帮助您估算实际距离，增加便利性。此外，当时社会的各种信息，包括行政和国防信息、经济、交通等，都是用符号来表达的。特别是，其特点是创建了与现代地图的图例相对应的单独的地图表，使得用户可以轻松快速地了解大量地理信息。我国古代地图的传统和金正浩的功绩韩国有着优秀的地图制作传统，从1402年（太宗2年）制作的《河一江里驿台国道图》中也可以看出这一点。 《东国大地图》是英祖时期郑尚基（1678-1752）用百利尺尺制作的，申庆俊（1712-1781）制作的。 《东国纪事图》等成为《大同纪事图》制作的基础。在制作《大同地图》之前，金正浩编写了《清九岛图》、《东野图》等国家地图手稿和《大同地图》等地理书籍。 《大同舆志图》就是通过整理这些地图制作传统而完成的。特别是，大同地图的一个特点是它是用木版印刷的，以便更多的人可以轻松携带和使用地图。韩国国家博物馆馆长柳洪俊表示：“这次展览将是一次宝贵的机会，可以通过与以前仅以书本形式呈现的大同地图相遇，直接体验金正浩的伟大成就和我们国家的美丽。”他补充说：“我希望您能够通过《大同舆地图》为我们古代地图的卓越性感到自豪，其中包含了朝鲜王朝科学和艺术的精髓。”演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

《The Origin》은 문신의 석고 원형을 그의 조각에서 형태가 태동하.en: 《The Origin》 illuminates Tao Moon’s plaster prototype as the first moment of form in his sculpture and as a complete work of art in itself. Generally, plaster prototypes are understood as an intermediate step toward the final work, but to Moon Jae-in, plaster prototypes were a condensation of the birth and creation process of a work of art, and had such special meaning that even in the last moments of his life, he requested a “Prototype Sculpture Exhibition” (June 3-July 31, 1995). These forms, which are infused with the artist's touch and time, are already filled with fullness even before they become completed sculptures. The plaster prototype is a pure white form that excludes color or material elements, and we encounter the first shape the artist conceived. In this pure and understated beauty, you can gain deep insight into his creative process and sensuously follow the depth of thought behind the shapes he pursued. The rhythm and volume of lines and surfaces flowing over the surface of the plaster, and the subtle tension created by light and shadow reveal the vitality of the work more clearly. In this way, the plaster prototype is a completed shape and at the same time a starting point for creation that allows for infinite variations, and can be said to be the source of the vibrant formative energy of the tattoo sculpture. Meanwhile, plaster prototypes require continuous preservation and management because they are greatly affected by time and the environment due to their material characteristics. In this exhibition, we will introduce examples of preservation of plaster prototypes of tattoos and examine how the works are managed after their creation and their meaning continues. This process makes you think about how the preservation of works of art connects time and memory to the present and the future. 《The Origin》 sheds new light on the meaning of plaster prototypes in the creative process of tattoos, and seeks to look deeply into his artistic world. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
《The Origin》은 문신의 석고 원형을 그의 조각에서 형태가 태동하.zh: 《起源》将陶月的石膏原型阐释为他雕塑中形式的第一个时刻，并且本身就是一件完整的艺术品。一般来说，石膏原型被理解为走向最终作品的中间步骤，但对文在寅来说，石膏原型是一件艺术品的诞生和创作过程的凝结，具有如此特殊的意义，以至于他在生命的最后时刻，要求举办“原型雕塑展”（1995年6月3日至7月31日）。这些充满了艺术家的笔触和时间的形式，在成为完整的雕塑之前就已经充满了丰满性。石膏原型是一种纯白色的形式，排除了颜色或材料元素，我们遇到了艺术家构想的第一个形状。在这种纯粹而低调的美感中，你可以深入了解他的创作过程，并感性地追随他所追求的形状背后的思想深度。石膏表面流动的线条与面的节奏与体积，以及光与影所产生的微妙张力，更清晰地揭示了作品的生命力。这样，石膏原型既是一个完整的形状，同时又是一个可以进行无限变化的创作起点，可以说是纹身雕塑充满活力的形成能量的源泉。同时，石膏原型因其材料特性，受时间和环境影响较大，需要持续保存和管理。在本次展览中，我们将介绍纹身石膏原型的保存实例，并探讨作品创作后的管理方式及其意义的延续。这个过程让你思考艺术品的保存如何将时间和记忆与现在和未来联系起来。 《起源》重新揭示了纹身创作过程中石膏原型的意义，并试图深入探讨他的艺术世界。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

스페이스나무 갤러리 오로라가 기획한 이번 박성열 초대전은 ‘존재는 어떻게.en: This Park Seong-yeol invitation exhibition, planned by Space Tree Gallery Aurora, begins with the question, ‘How is existence celebrated?’ The author deals with memory through shapes. It is not a frozen record of the past, but is still breathing and moving. The giant faces, animals, and monumental structures that appear on the screen stand in silence while staring at the audience and asking questions. This exhibition is a place to rethink the method of ‘commemoration’ and the meaning of ‘existence.’ The figures presented in this exhibition are not complete monuments. If traditional monuments were devices that stopped time by fixing heroes and victories with stone and metal, Park Seong-yeol's figures imply states of crack, erosion, and movement. The seemingly solid face is broken somewhere, and the symbolic figures are unstable, unable to maintain their center of gravity. It is closer to a face that has withstood the weight of time rather than an expression of victory. The author chooses a wavering state instead of a firm declaration, and a question instead of a straightforward message. Animal shapes such as horses, wolves, gorillas, and lions are also major motifs. They symbolize time, instinct, and the archetype of life before humans. If the human face represents history and civilization, animals are close to life itself. When two worlds overlap within one screen, existence is not fixed to one meaning but vibrates in multiple layers. Tensions between civilization and instinct, ideals and reality intersect tightly within pictorial space. Park Seong-yeol's screens are characterized by thick matiere. He repeats the process of piling up paint, scratching it, and adding it again, pushing up the screen like a sculpture. This physical property goes beyond simple texture and reveals the accumulation of time. Instead of a smoothly organized surface, the traces left behind testify to the ‘process’ rather than the ‘completion’. The form exists in a state of being both solid and alive, and still and yet moving. Rather than conveying a specific message, the author proposes a space that evokes the memories of each audience member. The moment we come face to face with a huge face, or the moment we receive the gaze of an animal approaching us directly, we ask ourselves: What remains as a memory? What is worth celebrating? And what kind of shape will we be left with? This invitational exhibition, planned by Space Tree Gallery Aurora, shows the possibility of expansion of contemporary figurative painting and is an opportunity to think anew about commemoration, memory, and the meaning of existence. Park Seong-yeol's fierce artist spirit, which has undergone constant changes and challenges, will be revealed more clearly through this exhibition. The question ‘How is existence celebrated?’ is the starting point of the exhibition and is a question that will be left to each viewer. Exhibition name: Park Seong-yeol Invitation Exhibition <Shapes that never sleep, how is existence celebrated> Participating artist: Park Seong-yeol Exhibition period: February 25, 2026 ~ March 23, 2026 Venue: Space Namu Gallery Aurora Inquiry: 055-374-3500 The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
스페이스나무 갤러리 오로라가 기획한 이번 박성열 초대전은 ‘존재는 어떻게.zh: 这次朴成烈邀请展由太空树画廊极光策划，以“如何庆祝存在？”这个问题开始，作者通过形状来处理记忆。它不是过去的冻结记录，而是仍在呼吸和移动。屏幕上出现的巨大面孔、动物和纪念性建筑静静地站着，凝视着观众并提出问题。这次展览是一个重新思考“纪念”的方式和“存在”的意义的地方。这次展览中呈现的人物并不是完整的纪念碑。如果说传统纪念碑是通过用石头和金属固定英雄和胜利来停止时间的装置，那么朴成烈的人物则意味着裂缝、侵蚀和运动的状态。看似坚固的面孔在某处破碎，象征性的人物也不稳定，无法保持重心。它更接近于经受住时间重压的面孔，而不是胜利的表情。作者选择了一种摇摆不定的状态而不是坚定的宣言，选择了一个问题而不是直截了当的信息。马、狼、大猩猩和狮子等动物形状也是主要图案。它们象征着时间、本能和人类之前的生命原型。如果说人的脸代表着历史和文明，那么动物则更接近生命本身。当两个世界在一个屏幕内重叠时，存在并不固定于一种意义，而是在多层中振动。文明与本能、理想与现实之间的张力在绘画空间中紧密地交织在一起。朴成烈的画面特点是厚重的材质。他重复着堆积颜料、刮擦、再添加的过程，将屏幕像雕塑一样推起。这种物理特性超越了简单的纹理，揭示了时间的积累。留下的痕迹不是平滑组织的表面，而是证明了“过程”而不是“完成”。形体以一种既坚固又生动、静止又动的状态存在。作者提出的不是传达特定信息，而是唤起每个观众记忆的空间。当我们与一张巨大的脸庞面对面的那一刻，或者当我们收到一只动物直接接近我们的目光的那一刻，我们问自己：什么是记忆？有什么值得庆祝的？我们会留下什么样的形状？此次邀请展由太空树极光画廊策划，展示了当代具象绘画拓展的可能性，也是一个重新思考纪念、记忆和存在意义的机会。朴成烈不断经历变化和挑战的强烈艺术家精神将通过本次展览得到更加清晰的展现。 “如何庆祝存在？”这个问题是展览的出发点，也是留给每个观众的问题。展览名称：朴成烈邀请展 <不眠的形状，如何庆祝存在> 参展艺术家：朴成烈 展览期间：2026年2月25日～2026年3月23日 地点：Space Namu Gallery Aurora 咨询：055-374-3500 表演/展览计划可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

What holds us back is not always what we see. It could be a structure, a relationship, a memory, or a silent tension. Both artists have explored these invisible forces in their own ways, and their work moves between space and emotion, order and anxiety, expanding the sensory realm that sculpture can reach. Information has studied architecture and sculpture together and has developed the language of sculpture with the concept of ‘space’ at the center for a long time. It is characterized by a three-dimensional sense that accepts structure, tension, flow, and even sound as part of the work through public sculptures and metal structures. Through two-dimensional and three-dimensional works that visualize the rhythm or frequency of music, he demonstrates a formative language that flexibly transcends sense, technology, structure, and flow. Choi Jeong-yoon has used symbolic materials such as swords, thread, salt, and flowers to sculpt human desire, power, and traces of time. Through the act of wrapping a sword with thread or sealing it with salt, one suppresses desires, seals emotions, and embodies the aesthetics of resentment. The formative language that combines symbolism and materiality creates tension along with strong interiority. 《What Holds Us》 creates a new balance by combining different aesthetic languages ​​such as structure and seal, space and desire, abstraction and symbolism. Through the work of the two artists, viewers will encounter the question ‘What holds us back?’ and their own answers. Gallery Sejul presents the two person exhibition What Holds Us featuring artists Chung Bowon and Choi Jeongyun, on view from February 26 to April 4, 2026. Bringing together two sculptors of different generations and artistic approaches, the exhibition poses a fundamental question about the forces that sustain and bind us. What holds us is not always something visible. It may take the form of structure, relationships, memory, or a silent tension that exists just beneath the surface. Through distinct yet resonant practices, both artists have long explored these invisible forces. Their works move fluidly between space and emotion, order and unease, expanding the sensory territory that sculpture can inhabit. Chung Bowon has developed his sculptural language around the concept of space, shaped by his background in both architecture and sculpture. His practice is characterized by an expanded spatial sensibility that embraces structure, tension, flow, and even sound as integral elements of form. 갤러리 세줄은 오는 2026년 2월 26일부터 04월 04일까지 작가 정.zh: Sejul 画廊将举办两人展览“什么让我们在一起 | 我们正在举办“什么让我们在一起”。通过将两位不同世代的艺术家的作品和表达方式并置在一个空间中，本次展览提出了关于维持和凝聚我们在一起的力量的本质的问题。阻碍我们前进的并不总是我们所看到的。它可以是一种结构、一种关系、一段记忆或一种无声的紧张。两位艺术家都以自己的方式探索了这些无形的力量，他们的作品游走于空间与情感、秩序与焦虑之间，拓展了雕塑所能触及的感官领域。信息长期将建筑与雕塑结合起来研究，发展了以“空间”概念为中心的雕塑语言。它的特点是具有三维感，通过公共雕塑和金属结构接受结构、张力、流动甚至声音作为作品的一部分。通过将音乐的节奏或频率可视化的二维和三维作品，他展示了一种灵活超越感觉、技术、结构和流动的形成语言。崔正润使用剑、线、盐、花等象征性材料来雕刻人类的欲望、力量和时间的痕迹。通过缠剑、盐封的行为，压抑欲望、封印情感，体现怨恨的美学。结合象征主义和物质性的形成性语言创造了张力和强烈的内在性。 《What Holds Us》通过结构与印记、空间与欲望、抽象与象征等不同美学语言的结合，创造出新的平衡。通过两位艺术家的作品，观众将遇到“是什么阻碍了我们？”的问题以及他们自己的答案。世珠画廊将于 2026 年 2 月 26 日至 4 月 4 日举办两人展览《What Holds Us》，展出艺术家 Chung Bowon 和 Choi Jeongyun。展览将两位不同年代和艺术方法的雕塑家聚集在一起，提出了一个关于支撑和束缚我们的力量的基本问题。支撑我们的并不总是可见的东西。它可能采取结构、关系、记忆或存在于表面之下的无声张力的形式。通过独特但引起共鸣的实践，两位艺术家长期以来一直在探索这些无形的力量。他们的作品在空间与情感、秩序与不安之间流畅地移动，扩大了雕塑可以栖息的感官领域。郑宝文围绕空间概念发展了他的雕塑语言，这是由他的建筑和雕塑背景塑造的。他的实践的特点是扩大了空间敏感性，将结构、张力、流动甚至声音作为形式的组成元素。通过金属结构和公共雕塑，以及将音乐节奏和自由形象化的二维和三维作品

“조각의 ‘평면적 기억’, 회화의 ‘확장된 공간 기억’이 결합될 때, 미.en: “When the ‘flat memory’ of sculpture and the ‘extended spatial memory’ of painting are combined, another possibility for artistic expression opens up.” ㅡSeongjin Yoon, Artist's Note 2025 Today, sculpture appears in a hybrid style with painting, installation art, performance, and video in terms of materials and expression techniques, and is expanding space and concepts through combination with other genres. Gallery JJ presents sculptor Seongjin Yoon’s solo exhibition <Seongjin Yoon: 2 Sides, 2 Perspectives>. Seongjin Yoon seeks a space beyond painting and sculpture and explores new experiences in contemporary sculpture. In a paradoxical approach that aims for a pictorial plane by minimizing the materiality and volume of traditional sculpture, the artist presents ‘2-face sculpture,’ an abstract object with two sides of a pictorial plane. It appears to combine pictorial experience with sculptural structure. This exhibition is the first to present the artist's works over the past four years since he returned to Seoul after a long period of living in Paris. It introduces new works such as <Folded Square> as well as representative 'double sculptures' of his work. The exhibition consists of about 20 standing works erected in a space and wall works using the wall surface. This exhibition highlights the unique formative methods he has thought and constructed and the uniqueness of his world of work based on the visual and perceptual experiences of visitors. Seongjin Yoon's abstract sculptures have expanded the boundaries of modern sculpture by exploring the point where the flatness of painting and the structure of sculpture meet, based on principles and formative sensibilities derived from geometric formative elements and calligraphy. His work, which has a formative structure that intersects the boundaries between painting and expression, goes beyond the physical space occupied by sculpture and raises questions about two-dimensionality and three-dimensionality by delicately revealing the spatial tension and layers of sensation that occur within the plane. The work, which the artist calls ‘painterly sculpture’ or ‘two-sided sculpture,’ is based on geometric abstract structures and moves between the genres of painting, sculpture, and installation. The method of juxtaposing two different pictorial surfaces on a single thin plate creates a tension between two-dimensional and three-dimensional, and encourages the work to be gradually completed through the viewer's movement and changes in gaze. In this way, the work goes beyond the dichotomous distinction of front and back, inside and outside, and creates another sensory space where atmospheres intersect between the two sides. Looking back, even in the past, art forms were not completely closed off from each other. Throughout the long history of Western sculpture, sculpture was not separated from and interacted with architecture and painting, but after the Renaissance, they became independent and took on autonomous forms, and over time, the competition between the forms only progressed in a way that proved itself to be a focused and powerful method. In modern art, the identity of sculpture has been constantly challenged, such as Naum Gabo, who tried to break away from the framework of traditional sculpture by minimizing mass and connecting the inside and outside with new materials, and Gwon Osang, who brought the medium of photography into sculpture and asked questions about the two-dimensional and three-dimensional aspects, which are big topics in sculpture. In the early 1990s, the artist was well known for his highly expressive works, expressing changes in values ​​and the era of chaos caused by the development of science, and denouncing the destruction of nature and the desolation of humanity. He continued the lineage of exploration of materiality in Korean art in the 1970s by cutting and combining silver aluminum plates, and his works are housed in major institutions at home and abroad, including the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Expressionist work, which emphasizes subjective sensibility and materiality, has gradually changed to the current geometric abstract form centered on balance and reason, raising curiosity about it. The reason for this seems to be found in the cultural atmosphere ingrained in Paris for nearly 20 years and the relationship between the cross-shaped formative work, the borrowing of the art history of the early 20th century, including Russian Constructivism, and, above all, the memory of the formative nature of calligraphy encountered from deep within the artist himself. — Lines, planes, space Geometrical abstract objects installed on the walls and floor of the exhibition hall continuously unfold the basic elements of form, lines and planes, not only within the plane but also as the structural form of sculpture.
“조각의 ‘평면적 기억’, 회화의 ‘확장된 공간 기억’이 결합될 때, 미.zh: “当雕塑的‘平面记忆’和绘画的‘扩展空间记忆’结合在一起时，艺术表达的另一种可能性就打开了。” ㅡ尹成镇，艺术家手记2025 如今，雕塑在材料和表现手法上与绘画、装置艺术、行为、视频等混合出现，并通过与其他流派的结合来扩展空间和概念。 JJ画廊呈现雕塑家Seongjin Yoon个展《Seongjin Yoon：2个侧面，2个视角》。 Seongjin Yoon 寻求绘画和雕塑之外的空间，探索当代雕塑的新体验。艺术家以一种矛盾的方式，通过最小化传统雕塑的物质性和体积来实现绘画平面，呈现了“双面雕塑”，这是一种具有绘画平面两侧的抽象物体。它似乎将绘画体验与雕塑结构结合起来。此次展览是艺术家长期旅居巴黎回到首尔四年来首次展出作品。介绍了《折叠的方块》等新作以及其代表作“双雕塑”。展览由约20件竖立在空间中的立式作品和利用墙面的墙壁作品组成。本次展览突出了他所思考和构建的独特的形成方法，以及基于参观者的视觉和感知体验的作品世界的独特性。 Seongjin Yoon 的抽象雕塑基于几何造型元素和书法的原则和造型情感，探索绘画的平面性和雕塑结构的交汇点，拓展了现代雕塑的界限。他的作品具有跨越绘画和表达界限的造型结构，超越了雕塑所占据的物理空间，通过微妙地揭示平面内发生的空间张力和感觉层次，提出了关于二维和三维的问题。该作品被艺术家称为“绘画雕塑”或“双面雕塑”，以几何抽象结构为基础，在绘画、雕塑和装置流派之间游走。将两个不同的画面并置在一块薄板上的方法创造了二维和三维之间的张力，并鼓励作品通过观看者的移动和目光的变化逐渐完成。这样，作品就超越了正面与背面、内部与外部的二元区分，创造出另一种两侧气氛交叉的感官空间。回顾过去，即使在过去，艺术形式之间也并非完全隔绝。纵观西方雕塑的悠久历史，雕塑与建筑和绘画并没有分离和互动，但在文艺复兴之后，它们变得独立并呈现出自主的形式，随着时间的推移，形式之间的竞争只会以一种被证明是一种集中而有力的方式进行。在现代艺术中，雕塑的身份不断受到挑战，比如Naum Gabo试图摆脱传统雕塑的框架，通过最小化质量并用新材料连接内部和外部，而Gwon Osang则将摄影媒介带入雕塑，并对二维​​和三维方面提出问题，这是雕塑中的大话题。 20世纪90年代初，艺术家以其极具表现力的作品而闻名，表达了科学发展带来的价值观的变化和时代的混乱，谴责自然的破坏和人类的荒凉。他通过切割和组合银色铝板，延续了20世纪70年代韩国艺术对物质性的探索，他的作品被收藏在国内外主要机构，包括国立现代艺术博物馆和大都会艺术博物馆。强调主观感性和物质性的表现主义作品逐渐转变为现在以平衡和理性为中心的几何抽象形式，引发人们的好奇心。其原因似乎在于巴黎近20年根深蒂固的文化氛围，以及十字形造型作品与20世纪初包括俄罗斯构成主义在内的艺术史的借鉴，以及最重要的是艺术家内心深处对书法造型本质的记忆之间的关系。 ——线、面、空间 展厅墙壁和地面上安装的几何抽象物体不断地展现出形式、线和面的基本要素，不仅在平面内，而且作为雕塑的结构形式。

맥화랑은 박영환(b.1998-) 작가의 개인전 《Immaterial: W.en: Mac Gallery is hosting artist Park Young-hwan's (b.1998-) solo exhibition 《Immaterial: What Remains》 from February 28th to March 28th. The artist, who works based on ink and Korean paper, has explored the layers of emotion, memory, and time through not only paintings but also performances and installations. This solo exhibition presents 17 new works of painting and ceramics, raising questions about the senses and states that remain after disappearance without completely disappearing.⠀ The black sphere that appears on the artist's screen is a formative unit that captures the process of life condensing, separating, and returning to flow. These shapes, arranged heterogeneously in landscapes or architectural spaces, disrupt the order of the representational landscape and visualize the multi-layered structure of life. The possibility of the spread and seepage of ink, accumulation and erasure, is in line with the sense of ‘immaterial’ that the artist focuses on, and the screen functions as a place to reveal the density of time rather than a space to reproduce objects.⠀ This exhibition unfolds at a time when the artist himself recognizes that his work is going through a transitional period. A point at which, while standing on an already formed formative language, we do not stop at repeating it but question its conditions again. The black sphere still exists on the screen, but the space in which it is placed, its density, and the way it is related are gradually changing.⠀ This exhibition asks: After the experience has passed, after the emotions have volatilized, after the work has passed one phase — what remains? And how does that remaining begin again at this moment? ⠀ GALLERY MAC is pleased to present 《Immaterial: What Remains》, a solo exhibition by Younghwan Park(b.1998-), on view from February 28 to March 28. Working primarily with ink and hanji (traditional Korean paper), the artist has explored layers of emotion, memory, and time not only through painting, but also through performance and installation. This exhibition presents 17 new works, including paintings and fired panel pieces, raising questions about sensations and states that do not entirely disappear even after vanishing.⠀ The black spheres that appear in the artist’s compositions function as formal units that embody the processes through which life condenses, separates, and flows once again. Positioned incongruously within landscapes or architectural spaces, these forms disrupt the order of representational scenery and visualize the multilayered structure of life. The spreading and permeation of ink, along with the possibilities of accumulation and erasure, resonate with the artist’s exploration of “immateriality.” Rather than serving as a site of depiction, the pictorial surface operates as a field where the density of lingering time becomes visible. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
맥화랑은 박영환(b.1998-) 작가의 개인전 《Immaterial: W.zh: Mac画廊将于2月28日至3月28日举办艺术家朴英焕（1998年生）个展《非物质：剩下的》。这位以水墨和韩纸为基础的艺术家不仅通过绘画、表演和装置探索了情感、记忆和时间的层次。本次个展呈现了17幅新的绘画和陶瓷作品，对消失后尚未完全消失的感官和状态提出质疑。⠀ 出现在艺术家画面上的黑色球体是一个造型单元，捕捉了生命凝结、分离和回归流动的过程。这些形状在景观或建筑空间中异质排列，破坏了代表性景观的秩序，并可视化了生活的多层结构。水墨的扩散与渗漏、堆积与擦除的可能性，符合艺术家所关注的“非物质”感，而屏幕的作用是揭示时间密度的场所，而不是再现物体的空间。⠀ 本次展览的展开正值艺术家本人认识到自己的作品正在经历一个过渡时期。在这一点上，当站在已经形成的形成性语言上时，我们不会停止重复它，而是再次质疑它的条件。黑球依然存在于画面中，但它所处的空间、它的密度、它的关联方式都在逐渐改变。⠀ 展览提出这样的问题：当经历过去之后，当情绪挥发之后，当作品经过一个阶段之后——还剩下什么？而此时此刻，剩下的一切又是如何开始的呢？ ⠀ GALLERY MAC 荣幸地呈现朴英焕（生于1998年-）的个展《非物质：剩下的》，将于2月28日至3月28日展出。艺术家主要以墨水和韩纸（韩国传统纸）为创作媒介，不仅通过绘画，还通过表演和装置探索情感、记忆和时间的层次。本次展览展出了17件新作品，包括绘画和烧制的面板作品，提出了关于即使消失后也不会完全消失的感觉和状态的问题。⠀ 出现在艺术家作品中的黑色球体作为形式单位，体现了生命凝聚、分离和再次流动的过程。这些形式在景观或建筑空间中的位置不协调，破坏了代表性风景的秩序，并可视化了生活的多层结构。水墨的扩散和渗透，以及堆积和擦除的可能性，与艺术家对“非物质性”的探索产生共鸣。绘画表面不是作为一个描绘的场所，而是作为一个场域，在这里，徘徊的时间的密度变得可见。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

갤러리그림손은 2026년 신진작가 공모전에 선정된 6명의 작가 김정희,.en: Gallery Grimson is holding an exhibition of six artists selected for the 2026 New Artist Contest: Kim Jeong-hee, Kim Hyeong-wook, Park Jeong-gyu, Min Lee, Jo Hee-ju, and Hwang Jeong-won. Every year, through a contest, we select artists who have had less than two solo exhibitions and who showcase novel and original formative artistry in their own style. This exhibition is an opportunity to see the questions and concerns of contemporary artists, as well as the world expressed in their own words, all in one place. A new perspective on the familiar, a method of expression that crosses boundaries, and a story that starts from personal experience and expands into universal sympathy are contained throughout the exhibition hall. Through this exhibition, we hope to provide a venue for artists with potential and potential to meet the audience in depth for the first time. Please join us for the moment when the new name becomes the starting point of how contemporary art will expand in the future. Artist Kim Jeong-hee uses Korean paper, which is a translucent threshold that passes light and the world through metaphor and lingering emotions, and explores the ‘other side’ between reveal and concealment, inside and outside, at that delicate boundary. Artist Kim Hyeong-wook reveals doubts about ‘complete reality’ in the uncertainty of the world created by the senses and the individual universe created by each person’s perception, and visualizes the state of energy and emptiness through the square blank space of the screen. Artist Park Jeong-gyu redefines past regrets and emotions and sublimates them into learning and memories, and through the harmony of dots and colors, he expresses his hope that they will eventually become a solid background in his work. Artist Minri explores the boundaries where inner senses intersect with external space and are revealed as forms, and works to leave room for viewers to imagine their own forms through screens where light and symbolic images interact. Artist Cho Hee-joo reinterprets disappearing spaces and childhood memories with warm colors and subjective perspectives to record ‘shapes of memories,’ and through this, conveys feelings of comfort and nostalgia. Artist Hwang Jeong-won fully embraces the moments of light, air, memory, and emotion that space evokes, and expresses the personal emotions that each space conveys through her work. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
갤러리그림손은 2026년 신진작가 공모전에 선정된 6명의 작가 김정희,.zh: Grimson画廊正在举办2026年新人艺术家大赛入选的六位艺术家的展览：金正熙、金亨旭、朴正奎、李敏、赵熙珠和黄正元。每年，我们都会通过竞赛选出举办过少于两次个展并以自己的风格展示新颖且原创的造型艺术的艺术家。这次展览提供了一个机会，让我们可以在一个地方看到当代艺术家的问题和担忧，以及用他们自己的语言表达的世界。对熟悉事物的新视角、跨界的表达方式、从个人经历出发延伸到普遍共鸣的故事，贯穿整个展厅。通过这次展览，我们希望为有潜力、有潜力的艺术家提供一个第一次深度与观众见面的场所。请加入我们，让新名字成为当代艺术未来拓展的起点。艺术家金正熙利用韩纸这种半透明的门槛，通过隐喻和缠绵的情感传递光线和世界，并在这种微妙的边界上探索暴露与隐藏、内部与外部之间的“另一面”。艺术家金亨旭在感官创造的世界的不确定性和每个人感知创造的个体宇宙中揭示了对“完整现实”的怀疑，并通过屏幕的方形空白空间可视化了能量和空虚的状态。艺术家朴正奎重新定义了过去的遗憾和情感，并将其升华为学习和记忆，并通过点与色彩的和谐，表达了他希望它们最终成为作品中坚实的背景的希望。艺术家 Minri 探索内部感官与外部空间相交并以形式展现的边界，并努力为观众留下空间，通过光和象征图像相互作用的屏幕来想象自己的形式。艺术家曹熙珠以温暖的色彩和主观视角重新诠释消失的空间和童年记忆，记录“记忆的形状”，并以此传达舒适和怀旧的感觉。艺术家黄正媛充分拥抱空间所唤起的光、空气、记忆和情感的瞬间，并通过她的作品表达每个空间所传达的个人情感。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

《깊고 깊은 숲으로: 도로시의 원더링》은 17세기 말 세일럼 마녀 재판*.en: 《Into the Deep, Deep Forest: Dorothy's Wondering》 begins with the Salem Witch Trials* in the late 17th century. Imagining the aftermath of Dorothy Good, a four-year-old girl who lost her mother in this incident, it brings back unrecorded times and sensations. Dorothy's journey of meeting various beings in the deep forest unfolds, blurring the boundaries between reality and fantasy. ‘Wondering’ in the exhibition title is not presented as aimless wandering, but as a process of recognizing the world after loss, establishing relationships, and reconstructing oneself. This exhibition asks what artist Stella Sujin sees and wants to leave behind through the act of painting. Through this, we are able to encounter the artist's perspective and flow of thoughts accumulated in the work. * Salem Witch Trials (1692–1693): A witch trial that took place in Salem, Massachusetts, USA, in which innocent people were sacrificed in a society full of conflict and prejudice. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
《깊고 깊은 숲으로: 도로시의 원더링》은 17세기 말 세일럼 마녀 재판*.zh: 《深入森林深处：多萝西的奇思妙想》始于 17 世纪末的塞勒姆女巫审判*。想象一下在这次事件中失去母亲的四岁女孩多萝西·古德（Dorothy Good）的后果，它会带回一些未记录的时光和感觉。多萝西在森林深处遇见各种生物的旅程展开，模糊了现实与幻想之间的界限。展览标题中的“徘徊”并不是漫无目的的徘徊，而是在失落之后认识世界、建立关系、重建自我的过程。本次展览询问艺术家Stella Sujin通过绘画行为看到了什么并想留下什么。借此，我们能够邂逅艺术家在作品中所积累的视角和思绪。 *塞勒姆女巫审判（1692-1693）：发生在美国马萨诸塞州塞勒姆的一场女巫审判，在充满冲突和偏见的社会中，无辜者被牺牲。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

설치작품은 공간을 작품의 일부로 사용하는만큼 자유로운 설치형태와 압도적인.en: As installation works use space as part of the work, they occupy the entire exhibition space with a free installation form and overwhelming scale, and have the characteristics of interacting with visitors. However, after the exhibition ends, it inevitably goes through a dismantling process and is stored in as compressed a form as possible. At this time, the dedicated storage box for artwork used to safely transport and store the work is called a ‘crate.’ Unlike simple shipping boxes, crates go through heat treatment and fumigation processes in accordance with international standards from the manufacturing stage to block the inflow of microorganisms and pests, and function as a small-scale preservation system designed to protect works from rapid changes in temperature and humidity as well as physical shock. New media works exist as data and variable hardware, not as fixed entities. Immaterial data is stored and implemented through storage and playback media, and with technological advancements, the format of storage and playback has changed dramatically as laser discs have transitioned to DVDs and DVDs have transitioned to digital files. This transition in media leads to the challenge of how to preserve the original form of new media works amidst the flow of technological change. Storage is the site of preservation and management where works are most privately protected before they are displayed. The museum's efforts to safely preserve and accurately represent works continue behind the scenes. This exhibition transparently shares the storage site by visualizing the functional cross-section of the museum's preservation management through a crate that condenses the huge scale of installation art and a new media storage system that preserves immaterial data. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
설치작품은 공간을 작품의 일부로 사용하는만큼 자유로운 설치형태와 압도적인.zh: 由于装置作品以空间作为作品的一部分，因此以自由的装置形式和压倒性的尺度占据了整个展览空间，并具有与参观者互动的特点。然而，展览结束后，它不可避免地要经历一个拆解过程，并以尽可能压缩的形式保存。此时，用于安全运输和储存作品的艺术品专用储存箱被称为“板条箱”。与简单的运输箱不同，板条箱从制造阶段就按照国际标准进行热处理和熏蒸过程，以阻止微生物和害虫的流入，并起到小型保存系统的作用，旨在保护作品免受温度和湿度快速变化以及物理冲击的影响。新媒体作品以数据和可变硬件的形式存在，而不是以固定的实体的形式存在。非物质数据是通过存储和播放介质来存储和实现的，随着技术的进步，存储和播放的格式发生了巨大的变化，如激光光盘过渡到DVD、DVD过渡到数字文件。媒体的这种转变带来了如何在技术变革的浪潮中保留新媒体作品原有形式的挑战。存储是保存和管理的场所，作品在展示之前在这里得到最私密的保护。博物馆在幕后继续努力安全地保存和准确地展示作品。本次展览通过一个浓缩了巨大装置艺术规模的箱子和保存非物质数据的新媒体存储系统，将博物馆保存管理的功能截面可视化，透明地共享存储场地。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

김대수는 청소년 시절부터 이어져 온 인간의 본질에 대한 질문으로부터 출발.en: Daesoo Kim is a photographer who starts from questions about the essence of humanity that have persisted since his youth and works on the subject of reflection on the passage of time and my existence. Living abroad for several years in the author's life further solidified his identity as a Korean. And in his quest for his roots, he becomes fascinated by bamboo, one of the Four Gentlemen (plum, chrysanthemum, orchid, and bamboo), a material that our ancestors enjoyed using in their arts and crafts. Artist Kim Dae-su, who says that the bamboo that extends straight even though it is hollow symbolizes the spirit of scholars who do not lose their upright spirit despite any hardships, adds that this ‘scholar spirit’ is a noble spirit that exists in all Koreans, and through his work, he provides enlightenment to the society and people who forget it and live today. In addition, the formative composition, use of black and white film, and working process in his work also stimulate Korean emotions by containing meanings such as the harmony of yin and yang and the white people. We hope that you will experience the scholarly spirit conveyed by the strong vitality and spiritual power of bamboo, which he has been exploring for a long time, through artist Kim Dae-su's solo exhibition [Luminous Sonata] held at Gallery Imazoo this March. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
김대수는 청소년 시절부터 이어져 온 인간의 본질에 대한 질문으로부터 출발.zh: 金大秀是一位摄影师，他从年轻时就一直存在的人性本质问题出发，以反思时间的流逝和我的存在为主题。作者在国外生活的几年进一步巩固了他作为韩国人的身份。在寻根的过程中，他对竹子着迷，竹子是四君子（梅、菊、兰、竹）之一，是我们的祖先在艺术和手工艺中喜欢使用的材料。艺术家金大洙表示，虽然空心但笔直延伸的竹子象征着即使遇到困难也不会失去正直精神的学者精神，他补充说，这种“学者精神”是所有韩国人都存在的崇高精神，他通过他的作品为忘记它并生活在今天的社会和人们提供启示。此外，其作品的造型构图、黑白胶片的运用、工作过程也包含阴阳和谐、白人等含义，激发了韩国人的情感。希望大家通过今年3月在Gallery Imazoo举办的艺术家金大洙个展《夜光奏鸣曲》，感受他长期以来不断探索的竹子的强大生命力和精神力量所传达的书香精神。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

. KIM WON KEUN 2026.3.5 - 4.25 부산 해운대구 해.en: . KIM WON KEUN 2026.3.5 - 4.25 Gallery Mare, Paradise Hotel New Wing B1, 296 Haeundae Beach-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan. . Kim Won-geun’s sculpture begins with ‘laughter.’ Instead of images of grand and sophisticated sculptures, he conveys the warmth of life through ordinary people that can be found anywhere around us. His human figures, made with colorful colors on a modern material called resin epoxy, just stand quietly without any special movements, but they make the viewer smile naturally. This exhibition, Spring of Spring, tells the story of the warm days of spring that finally arrived after a long, difficult and lonely winter. The characters in the work have stout bodies, bulging bellies, somewhat clumsy expressions, and unfashionable fashion. The first impression is that it is rough and rough, but the longer you look at it, the more strange feelings and affection seep into it. This is not a flashy protagonist, but an ordinary version of ourselves who has always remained on the periphery. Kim Won-geun gives a warm look to those who are easily alienated in modern society dominated by lookism. The large head, exaggerated body proportions, intense colors, and persistent surface texture give the characters a sense of vitality and reveal their lives and emotions more clearly. The author shines a spotlight on those who remained in supporting roles, and expresses the beauty of life as they each struggle in their own way. . . The writer says: “Our lives are like boxers fighting alone in a square ring. But the images of struggling youth are infinitely more beautiful. I wanted to express ‘portrait of youth’ through the stories of ordinary people, not some heroes or great people.” Kim Won-geun's sculptures convey hope through the purity of imperfect beings. Like spring that comes after a long winter, the characters in his works offer small messages of comfort and warm support to those of us living today. . . <Spring of Spring> is ultimately the story of the day of spring that arrives for all ordinary people. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220

KIM WON KEUN 2026.3.5 - 4.25 부산 해운대구 해.zh: 。 KIM WON KEUN 2026.3.5 - 4.25 釜山海云台区海云台海水浴场路 296 号天堂酒店新翼 B1 画廊 Mare。 。金元根的雕塑以“笑”开始。他不是用宏伟而复杂的雕塑形象，而是通过我们周围随处可见的普通人来传达生活的温暖。他的人物形象是用一种名为环氧树脂的现代材料制成的，色彩缤纷，只是静静地站着，没有任何特殊的动作，但却让观众自然地微笑。此次展览《春天的春天》讲述了在经历了漫长、艰难、孤独的冬天之后，终于迎来了温暖的春天的故事。作品中的人物身材粗壮，肚子鼓鼓的，表情有些笨拙，时尚不合时宜。第一印象是粗犷、粗犷，但看的时间越长，就越能渗透出奇异的感觉和情意。这不是一个浮华的主角，而是一个始终处于边缘的普通版的我们自己。金元根给那些在外貌主义主导的现代社会中容易被疏远的人以温暖的目光。硕大的头部、夸张的身体比例、浓烈的色彩、持久的表面纹理，赋予人物生机勃勃的感觉，更清晰地揭示他们的生活和情感。作者将目光聚焦在那些留在配角的人身上，表达了他们各自以自己的方式奋斗时的生活之美。 。 。作者说：“我们的生活就像拳击手在方环上孤军奋战。但奋斗的青春形象却无限美丽。我想通过普通人的故事来表达‘青春的肖像’，而不是一些英雄或伟人的故事。”金元根的雕塑通过不完美存在的纯洁传达希望。就像漫长的冬天过后的春天一样，他作品中的人物为我们今天的人们带来了安慰和温暖的支持。 。 。 《春天的春天》归根结底是关于所有普通人春天到来的日子的故事。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

[아기오리의 꿈]은 안데르센의 유명동화 <미운아기오리>를 가족뮤지컬로 재.en: [The Little Duckling's Dream] is a work that recreates Andersen's famous fairy tale The Ugly Duckling as a family musical. <The Ugly Duckling> ultimately has a happy ending for the main character, the Ugly Duckling. A happy story about a baby duckling who was mistreated for looking different but is actually a beautiful swan and not a duck. But suddenly, I wondered if this story would have a happy ending for the mother duck and her family who raised the ugly duckling as a child. Can we really find the answer in Blue Stage's <The Little Duckling's Dream> rather than Andersen's The Ugly Little Duckling? The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
[아기오리의 꿈]은 안데르센의 유명동화 <미운아기오리>를 가족뮤지컬로 재.zh: 《小鸭子的梦》是一部将安徒生著名童话《丑小鸭》改编成家庭音乐剧的作品。 《丑小鸭》最终为主角丑小鸭带来了幸福的结局。一个关于一只小鸭子的快乐故事，它因外表不同而受到虐待，但实际上是一只美丽的天鹅而不是鸭子。但突然，我想知道这个故事对于养育丑小鸭的鸭妈妈和她的家人来说是否会有一个幸福的结局。我们真的能在蓝台的《小鸭子的梦》而不是安徒生的《丑小鸭》中找到答案吗？演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

Back to the Nature 청화랑에서는 3월 전시로 김제민, 이경.en: Back to the Nature The Back to the Nature exhibition by artists Jemin Kim and Kyungha Lee will be held at Cheonghwarang in March. Authors Kim Je-min and Lee Kyeong-ha have a deep love for nature and have explored the relationship between nature and humans through different perspectives and media. Artist Kim Je-min uses gouache and oil painting to personify nature and objects, and depicts moments that we tend to overlook inadvertently into witty and warm scenes. It captures the expressions and emotions of nature in everyday life and offers visitors a new perspective. Artist Kyungha Lee uses charcoal and oil paint as her main materials to capture the images of modern people living in the vast nature. The contrast between the vast landscape and the characters makes us think about the fragility of human existence and at the same time the possibility of coexistence with nature. How far have we gone from nature, and how can we get back to it? We hope that you will take the time to reconsider the meaning of nature that you have forgotten in your daily life through the two authors' honest perspectives on nature. Title: Back to the Nature: Kim Je-min and Lee Kyung-ha Period: 26. 3.10-3.28 Location: Cheonghwarang, 4 Samseong-ro 147-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul Opening hours: Tue-Fri 11-18 p.m., Sat: 11-17 p.m. Inquiries: 02 543 1663 The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
Back to the Nature 청화랑에서는 3월 전시로 김제민, 이경.zh: 回归自然 艺术家 Jemin Kim 和 Kyungha Lee 的回归自然展览将于三月在清华郎举办。作者金济民和李庆河热爱自然，通过不同的视角和媒介探讨自然与人类的关系。艺术家金济民用水粉画和油画将自然和物体拟人化，将我们容易不经意忽视的瞬间描绘成诙谐而温暖的场景。它捕捉日常生活中自然的表情和情感，为游客提供新的视角。艺术家Kyungha Lee以木炭和油画为主要材料，捕捉现代人生活在广阔大自然中的形象。广阔的风景与人物的对比，让我们思考人类存在的脆弱性，同时思考与自然共存的可能性。我们离自然有多远，怎样才能回归自然？我们希望通过两位作者对自然的诚实视角，让你花时间重新思考你在日常生活中忘记的自然的意义。标题：回归自然：金济民和李庆河 期间：26. 3.10-3.28 地点：首尔江南区三成路 147 街 4 号青花郎 开放时间：周二至周五 11-18 p.m.，周六：11-17 p.m.咨询：02 543 1663 演出/展览日程可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

갤러리 플래닛은 2026년 3월 11일부터 4월 10일까지 김하나, 이예.en: Gallery Planet will host the two-person exhibition “The Last Dance with Me” by Hana Kim and Yeju Lee from March 11 to April 10, 2026. This exhibition straddles the border between painting and three-dimensionality, focusing on the method and process by which the work is formed rather than the objects of its reproduction. Hana Kim presents a painting work that emphasizes the density and rhythm of brushstrokes, and Yeju Lee presents a three-dimensional work that reveals the physical properties of plaster and the repetitive production process. Through this, we highlight the points where the physical rhythm and work language that the two artists have built are revealed. Hana Kim considers the flatness of painting as an important condition for her work, and reveals the artist's movement and sense of time through the density and rhythm of brushstrokes accumulated on the canvas. In his work, the screen is not simply a space to reproduce objects, but functions as a surface on which the experiences and traces of the body facing the world accumulate. Yeju Lee repeats the process of molding, adding, and carving out plaster, pushing the form to the point where the material's resistance is revealed. His three-dimensional work, which develops around organic curves and masses, evokes the potential of the body rather than directly reproducing the concrete body, and the color and texture of the surface bring together the accumulation of time and a non-linear sense. 《Last Dance with Me》 shows the attitude of the two artists toward their work. Here, ‘last’ does not mean the end, but is closer to a condensation point formed after repetition and accumulation and a moment of transition that prepares for the next movement. The attitude of pushing forward with work according to one's own rhythm rather than external standards or speed, and the artist's time to choose and handle each moment on his own form an important axis of this exhibition. This attitude is in line with the perspective of this exhibition, which focuses on the process and accumulation of work rather than the finished result. Rather than viewing the completed work only as a result, this exhibition seeks to read it as a record of movements accumulated during the work process. The artist's body, emotions, speed, and energy remain as traces on materials and surfaces, and the work is revealed as a condensed state of this process of selection, repetition, and push and pull. The exhibition presents this process as a metaphor for ‘dance’ and focuses on the flow of the artist’s movements and judgments that existed before the completed form. Through this, we will provide an opportunity to look at contemporary work from the perspective of process and accumulation, following Kim Hana and Lee Yeju's unique body language and subjective rhythm. 갤러리 플래닛은 2026년 3월 11일부터 4월 10일까지 김하나, 이예.zh: Gallery Planet将于2026年3月11日至4月10日举办Hana Kim和Yeju Lee两人展览“最后的与我共舞”。该展览跨越绘画和三维的边界，重点关注作品形成的方法和过程，而不是其复制的对象。 Hana Kim 呈现的绘画作品强调笔触的密度和节奏，Yeju Lee 呈现的三维作品揭示了石膏的物理特性和重复的生产过程。通过这一点，我们突出了两位艺术家所构建的身体节奏和工作语言的揭示点。 Hana Kim认为绘画的平面性是她作品的重要条件，并通过画布上积累的笔触的密度和节奏来揭示艺术家的运动和时间感。在他的作品中，屏幕不仅仅是一个再现物体的空间，而是作为一个表面，身体面对世界的经验和痕迹在其上积累。 Yeju Lee 重复塑造、添加和雕刻石膏的过程，将形状推向显示材料阻力的程度。他的三维作品围绕有机曲线和体量展开，唤起身体的潜力而不是直接再现具体的身体，表面的色彩和纹理带来了时间的积累和非线性感。 《与我共舞》展现了两位艺术家对自己作品的态度。这里的“最后”并不意味着结束，而是更接近于重复积累后形成的凝结点，以及为下一个动作做准备的过渡时刻。按照自己的节奏而不是外在的标准或速度推进作品的态度，以及艺术家自己选择和处理每个时刻的时间，构成了本次展览的一个重要轴。这种态度与本次展览的视角相一致，即关注作品的过程和积累，而不是最终的结果。这次展览并不只是将完成的作品视为结果，而是将其解读为工作过程中积累的动作记录。艺术家的身体、情感、速度和能量作为痕迹保留在材料和表面上，作品被揭示为这种选择、重复和推拉过程的浓缩状态。展览将这一过程作为“舞蹈”的隐喻来呈现，并重点关注在完成形式之前存在的艺术家动作和判断的流动。通过这一活动，我们将提供一个机会，沿着金荷娜和李艺珠独特的肢体语言和主观节奏，从过程和积累的角度来看待当代作品。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

이정빈 도예가는 불안과 안녕이라는 두 지점을 고민하여 동시대에 살아가는.en: Ceramic artist Jeongbin Lee has been contemplating the two points of anxiety and well-being, and has focused on the ‘Nyangupshin’ series, which is a guardian deity work that can fit modern people living in the same era. The work is sometimes shaped using local soil or traditional techniques, which is a result of the artist going further than inheriting technical traditions and reflecting that emotional elements are important in the formation of tradition in his work. This exhibition is mainly explained around two things. It deals with the author's method of conveying the writer's well-being in response to the widespread anxiety and concerns of the times, while also conveying the perspective of Korea's misfortune and ups and downs. The artist's core series, the 'Cat Up God' series, simultaneously shows the familiarity and closeness of a cat, as well as a kind of sublimity and dignity as a guardian deity. In addition, by looking at the traditional motifs of this guardian deity, such as fortune telling and family religious aspects, we ask the question of whether our perspective on ups and downs may have changed in the present era. Lifting and flying in the exhibition title traditionally refer to the flowing or flowing out of yin and yang energy, and ‘and side’ used together refers to the place where the guardian spirit object that exists next to our living space or area is placed. In this exhibition, the object of family faith, which has been placed as a relational object rather than a symbol of coercion and authority, is interpreted in a modern way, and at the same time, it shows that the attitude of Korea's faith for blessings and fortunes is not to hope for good things or good fortune in the moment, but to let the energy flow as it is. The artist's work provides comfort and solace in the anxiety of the current era, and at the same time, it is a guardian spirit that enables us to let go of what we let go and to face the incoming energy, regardless of mere luck and wealth. Originally, well-being is not a very happy or good state, but is like a wide river. Even though the wide river is flowing, it appears to be calm and unmoving. And yet it flows within it at its own pace. I hope that while viewing this exhibition, one of the guardian spirits will be placed in your heart and become a companion to help you enjoy a peaceful and well-being. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
이정빈 도예가는 불안과 안녕이라는 두 지점을 고민하여 동시대에 살아가는.zh: 陶瓷艺术家Jeongbin Lee一直在思考焦虑和幸福这两点，并专注于“Nyangupshin”系列，这是一件适合生活在同一时代的现代人的守护神作品。作品有时会使用当地的土壤或传统技术来塑造，这是艺术家超越继承技术传统的结果，并反映出情感元素在他的作品中形成传统的重要因素。本次展览主要围绕两件事进行阐述。它讲述了作者针对时代普遍的焦虑和忧虑而表达作者的幸福感的方法，同时也传达了韩国的不幸和坎坷的视角。艺术家的核心系列“猫上神”系列，既展现了猫的熟悉感和亲近感，又展现了作为守护神的一种崇高和尊严。此外，通过观察这位守护神的传统主题，例如算命和家庭宗教方面，我们提出一个问题：我们对盛衰的看法在当今时代是否可能发生了变化。展览名称中的“升”和“飞”传统上是指阴阳能量的流动或流出，而连用的“和侧”是指放置存在于我们的居住空间或区域旁边的守护神物体的地方。在本次展览中，家庭信仰这个被置于关系对象而不是强制和权威象征的对象被以现代的方式诠释，同时也表明了韩国信仰对福祉和财富的态度不是希望当下有好事或好运，而是让能量就这样流动。艺术家的作品为当今时代的焦虑提供了安慰和慰藉，同时也是一种守护精神，让我们能够放下已经放下的东西，面对即将到来的能量，无论运气和财富如何。本来，幸福并不是一种非常幸福或美好的状态，而是像一条宽阔的河流。尽管宽阔的河流在流淌，但它却显得平静，一动不动。然而它却以自己的节奏在其中流动。希望您在观看本次展览的同时，能将其中一位守护神安放在您的心中，成为您的陪伴，让您享受一份宁静与幸福。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

\"이 세계에서 우리가 안전할지 잘 모르겠어.\" 스포츠가 언제나 공정한.en: “I’m not sure we’re safe in this world.” Sports aren't always fair. Although it creates the illusion of fairness through strict rules and refereeing processes, various bodies have been ‘eliminated’ from sports under the name of fairness. I keep hesitating in front of the world I will live in from now on. Nevertheless, athletes do not give up on what they love. They embrace each other's concerns and find a way to exist together on the court. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220

This exhibition encompasses the artist's entire work, from his early works to his recent works, and consists of various media such as installation, sculpture, and painting. 미술관의 '얼굴'인 소장품은 수장고에 보존된 과거의 예술에 머무르지 않는.en: The collection, which is the ‘face’ of the museum, is not limited to past art preserved in storage. The collection is living art that meets us again now and creates new meaning. In the layers of time, the collection asks the question, “What have we done and what should we do?” and makes us think about our past and future together. The 20th anniversary of the Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art, Flowing and Accumulating, looks back on the museum's past with 125 pieces from its collection and looks at its future direction. The title “flowing and accumulating” is a metaphor for the process of our thoughts and questions accumulating and expanding over time. This encompasses the 20 years of Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art and the meaningful moments the collection will create with visitors in the future. This exhibition does not list the past, but focuses on the moment when memories of the past are summoned to the present and acquire meaning. The collections, which were born at different times and collected in the museum, meet visitors here and now, creating new moments. This encounter leads to the museum's essential questions: “How do art and life meet?” and “How does an art museum connect visitors and art?” The exhibition unfolds the landscape where art and life meet through five questions, ranging from the fundamental beginnings of art to the scenery of our daily lives, memories of things that are forgotten, and solidarity and practice. When various ‘we’ with different backgrounds and experiences build up our own thoughts on this question, the exhibition acquires richer meaning. "Does art ( ) begin?" - About art that breaks down and expands boundaries "Do we live ( )?" - About the colorful aspects of everyday life and the trajectory of life "Do we remember ( )?" - About recalling forgotten memories to the present and remembering them together "Does art ( ) together?" - About connecting in the process and the meaning of 'together' "Do I practice ( )?" - About social practice examined through the attitude of artists The parentheses in the question are left blank. Let’s fill in the blanks and listen to the story that art tells. In particular, the last question highlights the attitude and practice adopted by an artist among members of society, focusing on the work of artist Kim Jeong-heon donated in 2024. This journey, which starts with art, discovers ‘us’, and then discovers ‘me’ again in art, does not lead to a single answer. Rather, it leads to more questions. The exhibition is completed only when the ‘now’ moment when the collection and the visitor meet, and the visitor’s thoughts are added. I hope this will be a time for you to reflect on yourself and your surroundings through the encounter with art that flows and accumulates. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
미술관의 '얼굴'인 소장품은 수장고에 보존된 과거의 예술에 머무르지 않는.zh: 藏品是博物馆的“脸面”，不仅限于储存的过去的艺术品。该系列是活生生的艺术，现在再次与我们见面并创造新的意义。在时间的层层递进中，藏品提出这样的问题：“我们做了什么，我们应该做什么？”并让我们一起思考我们的过去和未来。京畿道现代美术馆成立20周年之际，《流动与积累》以馆藏的125件作品回顾了美术馆的过去，展望了美术馆的未来发展方向。标题“流动和积累”隐喻了我们的思想和问题随着时间的推移积累和扩展的过程。这涵盖了京畿道现代艺术博物馆的20年历史以及藏品未来将与参观者一起创造的有意义的时刻。本次展览并不罗列过去，而是关注过去的记忆被召唤到当下并获得意义的那一刻。这些诞生于不同时期并收藏于博物馆的藏品此时此地与参观者见面，创造新的时刻。这次相遇引出了博物馆的基本问题：“艺术与生活如何相遇？”以及“美术馆如何连接游客和艺术？”展览通过五个问题，从艺术的起源到日常生活的风景、被遗忘的事物的记忆、团结与实践，展现了艺术与生活相遇的风景。当不同背景、不同经历的“我们”对这个问题建立起自己的思考时，展览就获得了更丰富的意义。 “艺术开始了吗？” - 关于打破和扩展界限的艺术“我们生活吗（）？” - 关于日常生活的丰富多彩和生命的轨迹“我们还记得（ ）吗？” - 关于将遗忘的记忆回忆到现在并一起记住“艺术（ ）在一起吗？” - 关于过程中的联系和“在一起”的含义“我练习（）吗？” ——关于通过艺术家的态度审视社会实践问题中的括号留空。让我们一起填补空白，聆听艺术讲述的故事。特别是最后一个问题，重点关注了艺术家金正宪2024年捐赠的作品，凸显了艺术家在社会成员中所采取的态度和实践。这段从艺术开始，发现“我们”，然后在艺术中再次发现“我”的旅程，并没有得出单一的答案。相反，它会带来更多问题。只有当藏品与参观者相遇的“当下”时刻，加上参观者的想法时，展览才算完成。我希望这将是您通过与流动和积累的艺术的邂逅来反思自己和周围环境的时刻。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

한국과 프랑스를 오가며 양국의 문화예술을 양분 삼아 독자적인 예술 세계를.en: This is an exhibition that introduces the works of Bang Hye-ja (1937-2022), who traveled back and forth between Korea and France and built an independent world of art based on the culture and arts of both countries. In this exhibition, which provides a comprehensive view of the life, worldview, and expression method of the artist who has used ‘light’ as a source of inspiration throughout his life, and explores its significance, you can examine the process of various pictorial experiments and insights. 한국과 프랑스를 오가며 양국의 문화예술을 양분 삼아 독자적인 예술 세계를.zh: 本次展览介绍了方惠子（1937-2022）的作品，她往返于韩国和法国之间，以两国文化艺术为基础构建了独立的艺术世界。作为2026年纪念韩法建交140周年的活动之一，本次展览介绍了以女性艺术家身份展示早期抽象艺术作品的方慧子各个时期的主要作品，以及韩国国立现代美术馆收藏的未在韩国引进的法国作品。在本次展览中，您可以全面审视艺术家一生以“光”为灵感来源的生活、世界观和表达方式，并探讨其意义，并审视各种绘画实验和感悟的过程。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

J.B accidentally learns a secret about a public well and becomes caught up in a fight between Ashley Queens, the eldest son of the Queens family who monopolizes it, and Edmund Queens, who has lost all of his inheritance. Jack Solo, who guards the town's salon, which went bankrupt as water prices soared, looks as precarious as a withered cactus. Jack Solo heals J.B.'s injured leg and receives a bullet in return. 공용 우물이 말라버린 ‘뉴 밀리언 골드 타운’에 희대의 탕아 ‘J.B’가.zh: 罕见的浪子“J.B”来到公共井已经干涸的“新百万金镇”。 J.B 无意中得知了一口公共水井的秘密，并卷入了垄断公共水井的皇后家族长子阿什利·奎恩斯 (Ashley Queens) 与失去全部遗产的埃德蒙·奎恩斯 (Edmund Queens) 之间的斗争。镇上的沙龙因水价飙升而破产，守卫杰克·索罗看上去就像枯萎的仙人掌一样岌岌可危。杰克·索罗治愈了 J.B. 受伤的腿，并收到了一颗子弹作为回报。那些只关心自己利益和安全的人被追赶，一场血腥的战斗爆发了，在漫长的等待结束时，大自然的反叛开始了。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

모래로 그림을 그리는 샌드아트와 뮤지컬이 결합된 새로운 공연 양식이며,.zh: 是沙画与音乐剧相结合的一种新的表演形式。这是一部青春治愈音乐剧，通过详细描绘现实的校园生活以及青少年围绕欺凌和校园暴力的心理，帮助人们了解自己和彼此。通过这项工作，我们希望传播一种相互理解、相互温暖、同情和沟通的文化。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

«이것은 개념미술이 (아니)다»는 한국현대미술의 흐름 속에서 물질적 형식.en: «This is (not) conceptual art» is an exhibition that highlights conceptual art that focuses on concepts, language, process, and context rather than material form or visual completion in the flow of Korean contemporary art. In particular, this exhibition focuses on the linguistic turn in art and revisits works that have constantly reflected on the essence and reality of art through subtopics such as objects and language, language and behavior, measurement and guidance, and reality and institutional criticism. In addition, we hope to provide an opportunity to discuss the contemporaneity of Korean contemporary art by examining the conceptual trends of post-war art in the 1990s, which developed amidst advanced capitalism and rapid social and political changes, along with the trends of previous generations of art. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
«이것은 개념미술이 (아니)다»는 한국현대미술의 흐름 속에서 물질적 형식.zh: “这是（不是）观念艺术”是一个强调观念艺术的展览，它关注韩国当代艺术流程中的概念、语言、过程和语境，而不是物质形式或视觉完成。本次展览特别关注艺术的语言转向，通过物体与语言、语言与行为、测量与引导、现实与制度批判等副主题，重新审视那些不断反思艺术本质与现实的作品。此外，我们希望通过审视1990年代战后艺术的观念趋势（在先进的资本主义和快速的社会和政治变革中发展起来）以及前几代艺术的趋势，提供一个讨论韩国当代艺术当代性的机会。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

과천관 개관 40주년을 맞이하여 미술관을 새롭게 밝히고, 관람객들이 미술.en: To celebrate the 40th anniversary of the opening of the Gwacheon Museum, we are promoting a series of site-specific installation projects with the theme of ‘light’ to brighten the museum and allow visitors to experience deeper artistic immersion both inside and outside the museum. In addition to the new collection, James Turrell's “Imaginations, Wide Rectangular Curved Surface,” the museum collaborates with contemporary artists, architects, and designers at home and abroad, including Jeong-ah Koo, A-young Kim, Philippe Parreno, and Ivan Navarro, to install their works in major spaces inside and outside the museum, reinterpreting the space based on the sense of place of the Gwacheon building. Through this, we would like to propose a new sensory experience using light as a medium. In particular, taking advantage of the unique characteristics of the Gwacheon Museum as an art museum within nature, we plan to implement a space program inside and outside the museum in which art, nature, and thinking organically connect. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
과천관 개관 40주년을 맞이하여 미술관을 새롭게 밝히고, 관람객들이 미술.zh: 为庆祝果川博物馆开馆40周年，我们正在推广一系列以“光”为主题的特定场域装置项目，以点亮博物馆，让游客在博物馆内外体验更深层次的艺术沉浸。除了詹姆斯·特雷尔的新藏品“想象，宽矩形曲面”之外，博物馆还与国内外当代艺术家、建筑师和设计师合作，包括Jeong-ah Koo、A-young Kim、Philippe Parreno、Ivan Navarro，将他们的作品安装在博物馆内外的主要空间中，以果川建筑的场所感为基础重新诠释空间。通过这一点，我们想提出一种以光为媒介的新感官体验。特别是，利用果川博物馆作为自然美术馆的独特特征，我们计划在博物馆内外实施艺术、自然和思维有机结合的空间计划。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

이대원(1921-2005)은 김환기, 박수근, 장욱진, 천경자와 더불어.en: Lee Dae-won (1921-2005) is a representative artist of Korean modern and contemporary art, along with Kim Hwan-ki, Park Soo-geun, Jang Wook-jin, and Cheon Kyeong-ja. In his teens, he was already selected for the Joseon Art Exhibition three times in a row, and he held a total of 19 solo exhibitions, starting with his first at the age of 36. However, research and exhibitions that examined Lee Dae-won's world of work from an art historical perspective were insufficient. Although he was widely known as a landscape painter who mainly painted ‘orchards,’ his early painting occupies a very unique position in the Korean art world at the time. After liberation, he had a significant impact on the Korean art world as a whole, including the formation of Korean aesthetic theory, operation of the Bando Gallery, and serving as president of Hongik University. This exhibition sheds new light on Lee Dae-won's life and art in three dimensions by examining the background and historical context of his work and closely depicting the process leading up to the orchard painting, a typical example of Lee Dae-won's work. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
이대원(1921-2005)은 김환기, 박수근, 장욱진, 천경자와 더불어.zh: 李大元（1921-2005）是与金焕基、朴秀根、张旭镇、千景子齐名的韩国现当代艺术代表艺术家。十几岁的时候，他就已经连续3次入选朝鲜美术展，从36岁第一次举办个展开始，总共举办了19次个展。但是，从艺术史的角度审视李大元的作品世界的研究和展览还不够。尽管他被广泛认为是一位主要画“果园”的山水画家，但他早期的绘画在当时的韩国艺术界占有非常独特的地位。解放后，他对整个韩国艺术界产生了重大影响，包括韩国美学理论的形成、坂东画廊的运营以及担任弘益大学校长。本次展览通过考察李大源作品的背景和历史脉络，近距离描绘李大源作品典型代表——果园画的创作过程，从三个维度对李大源的生活和艺术进行了新的阐释。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

한국을 대표하는 설치미술가 서도호의 대규모 개인전으로, 초기작부터 주요작.en: This is a large-scale solo exhibition by Korea's leading installation artist Do-ho Suh, encompassing his artistic world from early works to major works to ongoing projects, and illuminating the artist's conceptual foundation and practical expansion in a three-dimensional way. The author has been deepening the issues of spatial memory and identity, focusing on the themes of migration and residence, individuals and communities, and is further expanding the scope of his creativity based on multidisciplinary research. Through this exhibition, which redefines the world of his work, we hope to raise the status of Korean contemporary art and at the same time provide an experience in which his themes are newly transferred and expanded within each viewer's narrative. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
한국을 대표하는 설치미술가 서도호의 대규모 개인전으로, 초기작부터 주요작.zh: 这是韩国著名装置艺术家徐道浩的大型个展，涵盖了他从早期作品到主要作品再到正在进行的项目的艺术世界，并以三维方式阐释了艺术家的观念基础和实践拓展。作者不断深化空间记忆与身份问题，聚焦迁徙与居住、个人与社区等主题，并在多学科研究的基础上进一步拓展创作范围。通过这次重新定义他的作品世界的展览，我们希望提高韩国当代艺术的地位，同时提供一种体验，让他的主题在每个观众的叙述中得到新的转移和扩展。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

1970년대 인쇄 출판 분야에 한글 가로쓰기가 도입된 이후 그래픽 디자인.en: This exhibition traces the history of graphic design since the introduction of horizontal Hangul writing in the printing and publishing field in the 1970s. The activities of designers who have studied the relationship between text and images in an environment transitioning from analog to digital will be reconstructed by era. The exhibition presents experimental attempts that cross the material and non-material world through the revival of phototypesetting and offset printing technology in the 1970s and 1980s, the transition to graphic tools and the web environment in the 1980s and 1990s, and today. This exhibition is an attempt to expand the base of Korean art by examining the dynamic relationship between technological development and visual culture within the flow of graphic design practice. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
1970년대 인쇄 출판 분야에 한글 가로쓰기가 도입된 이후 그래픽 디자인.zh: 本次展览追溯了自 20 世纪 70 年代印刷和出版领域引入水平韩文书写以来平面设计的历史。在从模拟向数字过渡的环境中研究文本和图像之间的关系的设计师的活动将被时代重构。展览通过20世纪70年代和1980年代照相排版和胶印技术的复兴、20世纪80年代和1990年代以及今天向图形工具和网络环境的过渡，呈现了跨越物质和非物质世界的实验性尝试。本次展览试图通过审视平面设计实践流程中技术发展与视觉文化之间的动态关系来扩大韩国艺术的基础。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

한국전쟁 이후, 파리를 ‘현대예술의 수도’로 여긴 적지 않은 한국의 미술.en: After the Korean War, many Korean artists who considered Paris the ‘capital of modern art’ moved to France. In the Paris art world, which competed with New York for the center of international art after World War II and sought to revive the glory of modernism, they interacted with artists from all over the world, experienced a variety of new contemporary art, and built their own world. This exhibition illuminates in three dimensions the art world of Korean artists who moved to Paris in the 1950s and 1970s, starting with Lee Jong-woo, who became the first Korean artist to move to Paris in 1925. The exhibition explores the diverse art world of Taoist and Buddhist artists who pursued modernization by seeking national identity in unfamiliar places, or expanded the boundaries of art through exploration of new themes and experimentation with media, and examines the meaning and value of their lives and art as strangers. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
한국전쟁 이후, 파리를 ‘현대예술의 수도’로 여긴 적지 않은 한국의 미술.zh: 朝鲜战争后，许多将巴黎视为“现代艺术之都”的韩国艺术家移居法国。在二战后与纽约争夺国际艺术中心、寻求重振现代主义辉煌的巴黎艺术界，他们与世界各地的艺术家互动，体验各种新的当代艺术，构建自己的世界。本次展览从三个维度阐释了20世纪50年代和1970年代移居巴黎的韩国艺术家的艺术世界，从1925年第一位移居巴黎的韩国艺术家李钟宇开始。展览探讨了道教和佛教艺术家在陌生的地方寻求民族认同以追求现代化，或通过探索新主题和媒体实验来扩展艺术边界的多元化艺术世界，并审视他们生命和生活的意义和价值。艺术如陌生人。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

국내 대표작가들의 작품전을 기획, 전시하는 93뮤지엄93뮤지엄은 1990.en: 93 Museum 93 Museum, which plans and displays works by leading domestic artists, started as Gallery Focus in Cheongdam-dong, Seoul in 1990. In 2004, the People Art Museum 93 opened in Paju Heyri Art Village by compiling art pieces and various historical materials related to people, and the gallery was moved to the museum annex, where exhibitions of works by leading domestic artists are being planned and displayed. Gallery Focus in Cheongdam-dong, Seoul, exhibited contemporary art works by Korea's older and younger artists, as well as ancient works of art such as ancient paintings and ceramics, and consistently discovered and introduced works by leading Vietnamese artists. In 2007, the Seoul branch of Gallery Focus, operated in conjunction with Paju Heyri Gallery Focus, was opened in Samseong-dong and is exhibiting works by leading Korean masters, as well as works by emerging and promising artists and works by leading Vietnamese artists. 93 Museum, Gallery Focus, and Gallery Focus are demonstrating the qualities of professional art dealers by taking advantage of each other's characteristics and complementing each other.
국내 대표작가들의 작품전을 기획, 전시하는 93뮤지엄93뮤지엄은 1990.zh: 93博物馆 93博物馆于1990年在首尔清潭洞作为Gallery Focus开始策划和展示国内顶尖艺术家的作品。2004年，人民艺术博物馆93在坡州Heyri艺术村开设，汇集了与人民有关的艺术作品和各种历史资料，画廊搬到了博物馆别馆，在那里策划和展示国内顶尖艺术家的作品。位于首尔清潭洞的 Gallery Focus 展出了韩国老一辈和年轻艺术家的当代艺术作品，以及古代绘画和陶瓷等古代艺术作品，并不断发现和介绍越南领先艺术家的作品。 2007年，与Paju Heyri Gallery Focus联合运营的Gallery Focus首尔分店在三成洞开业，展出韩国顶尖大师的作品，以及新兴和有前途的艺术家以及越南顶尖艺术家的作品。 93美术馆、焦点画廊、焦点画廊正在优势互补、优势互补，展现专业艺术品经销商的品质。

AK&amp;기흥은 지하 1층부터 지상 6층까지 약 1만 8,400평 규.en: AK & Giheung is a complex shopping mall with an area of ​​approximately 18,400 pyeong, from the 1st basement level to the 6th floor above ground. It is directly connected to exits 3, 4, and 9 of Giheung Station, where the Suin-Bundang Line and Yongin Light Rail pass, making it highly accessible. Lotte Premium Food Market is located on the first basement floor, and lifestyle brands such as fashion, beauty, and F&B and experiential content are located on each floor on the upper floors. It is characterized by strengthening kids and family stores and convenience facilities to reflect the regional characteristics of a high proportion of young couples and families living there.

AK플라자 광명점은 경기도 광명시 광명역 인근에 자리한 복합 쇼핑몰로,.en: AK Plaza Gwangmyeong Branch is a complex shopping mall located near Gwangmyeong Station in Gwangmyeong-si, Gyeonggi-do, where you can enjoy shopping, dining, and culture all in one place. The ‘Urban Grove’ concept emphasizes the harmony between nature and the city, and Korea’s largest kinetic art installation adds visual fun. It is suitable for families as it has a variety of brands including fashion, living, food and beverages. The open playground on the 3rd floor is equipped with various facilities and programs and can be used for free, making it a great place to visit with children.

AK플라자 금정점은 패션·뷰티·라이프스타일과 F&amp;B가 어우러진 복.en: AK Plaza Geumjeong Branch is a shopping complex that combines fashion, beauty, lifestyle, and F&B. Golf, sports, and children's stores are located on the first basement floor, and cosmetics, lifestyle brands, and Megabox are located on the first floor. The Geumjeong branch's landmark, a large hand heart bearbrick sculpture, is installed on the second floor, making it a must-see photo spot for visitors. You can also take a leisurely break at the rooftop garden and cafe.

수원역에 위치한 AK플라자 수원은 쇼핑과 문화, 엔터테인먼트가 공존하는.en: AK Plaza Suwon, located at Suwon Station, is Suwon's representative cultural complex where shopping, culture, and entertainment coexist. It is connected to Subway Line 1, the Suin Bundang Line, and the Bus Transfer Center, so it can be conveniently visited from anywhere in the country. Featuring a variety of cultural and character content, including popular fashion and beauty brands, Megabox Movie Theater, Gundam Base, and Acorn Forest, as well as large-scale dining stores such as Ashley Queens, Outback Steak House, and Cymbidium, it is loved as Suwon's representative cultural attraction where you can stay and enjoy all day with family, friends, and lovers.

가리왕산 케이블카는 대한민국 100대 명산에 속하고 2018 평창동계올림.en: Gariwangsan Cable Car is located on Gariwangsan Mountain, which is one of the top 100 famous mountains in Korea and successfully hosted the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics. Gariwang Mountain has been renovated so that many citizens can enjoy it even after the Olympics are over. At the top of the cable car, various convenience facilities of 512.5㎡ are installed, including a 2,400㎡ ecological exploration deck road, an unmanned agricultural product store (gift shop), a VR experience center, a DID video theater, a customer rest area, a cafe 156 days, and a moonlight photo zone. People of all ages and the disabled and those with mobility issues can easily access it without any inconvenience. The cable car may close early or close without prior notice for safety reasons such as weather conditions, so it is best to check in advance before visiting.
가리왕산 케이블카는 대한민국 100대 명산에 속하고 2018 평창동계올림.zh: 加里王山缆车位于韩国百大名山之一的加里王山，曾成功举办过2018年平昌冬奥会。加里旺山经过整修，让许多市民即使在奥运会结束后也能享受到这里的乐趣。缆车顶部设置了512.5平方米的各类便民设施，包括2400平方米的生态探索甲板道、无人农产品店（礼品店）、VR体验中心、DID视频影院、顾客休息区、156天咖啡馆、月光拍照区等。所有年龄段的人以及残疾人和行动不便的人都可以轻松访问它，不会造成任何不便。出于天气状况等安全原因，缆车可能会提早关闭或关闭而不另行通知，因此最好在参观前提前查询。

청계산 자락에 위치한 가원미술관은 한국 수채화협회와 연계되어 있고, 수채.en: Gawon Art Museum, located at the foot of Cheonggyesan Mountain, is affiliated with the Korea Watercolor Association and is an art museum specializing in watercolor painting. Opened in 2003, this museum was built as a two-story building in European style. On the first basement floor, there is the Gawon Academy and Atelier, where watercolor and oil painting classes are held. The first floor is the first exhibition room and a lounge, and the second floor is the second exhibition room, the third exhibition room, and the curator's room. There is a cafe inside the museum, and if you order a drink, you can receive a 50% discount on admission. Gawon Art Museum is also famous for its beautiful garden, as its name Gawon (佳苑, beautiful garden) suggests. Gawon Art Museum is also frequently used as a filming location for dramas, and dramas such as The Fugitive, War of the Roses, Tale of the New Gisaeng, Wild Romance, and Secret were filmed here.
청계산 자락에 위치한 가원미술관은 한국 수채화협회와 연계되어 있고, 수채.zh: 位于清溪山脚下的加文美术馆，隶属于韩国水彩画协会，是一家专门研究水彩画的美术馆。该博物馆于2003年开馆，为一栋欧式两层建筑。地下一层有高文学院和工作室，举办水彩画和油画课程。一层为第一展厅和休息室，二层为第二展厅、第三展厅和馆长室。博物馆内有一家咖啡馆，如果点饮料可以享受入场50%的折扣。正如其名“佳苑”一样，加文美术馆也因其美丽的花园而闻名。高园美术馆也经常被用作电视剧的拍摄地，《逃亡者》、《玫瑰战争》、《新妓女传》、《狂野罗曼史》、《秘密》等电视剧都曾在此拍摄。

북한강을 따라 아름다운 길을 드라이브하다 보면 양수리에서 청평호수로 가는.en: If you drive along the beautiful road along the Bukhangang River, you will find Gail Art Museum about halfway from Yangsu-ri to Cheongpyeong Lake. Kang Geon-guk, director of Gail Art Museum, the first private art museum in Gapyeong-gun, has been working as an architect and interior designer for 30 years. He opened in 2003 and has been holding regular concerts once a month at the exhibition hall or art hall as of 2020. He is planning concerts with a variety of genres, including popular music, jazz, and classical music. In addition, starting from the idea that music, along with art, is the best character education for children, we continue to hold art experience classes, especially for children in Gapyeong, a culturally underprivileged area. Gail Art Museum's exhibitions are planned as family-oriented exhibitions to differentiate themselves from large art museums. The Gail Art Museum, which means that every day of the museum's visitors will be a "beautiful day," is a complex cultural space equipped with a variety of facilities, including an art hall where domestic and foreign art works are exhibited and various performances such as chamber music and jazz are held, and an outdoor performance hall where the public can directly participate in customized concerts.
북한강을 따라 아름다운 길을 드라이브하다 보면 양수리에서 청평호수로 가는.zh: 沿着北汉江美丽的道路行驶，在从杨水里到清平湖的半路上就能找到盖尔美术馆。加平郡第一家私立美术馆盖尔美术馆馆长姜建国从事建筑师和室内设计师工作已有30年。他于2003年开业，截至2020年，每月一次在展览馆或艺术馆定期举办音乐会。他正在策划各种流派的音乐会，包括流行音乐、爵士乐、古典音乐。此外，本着音乐与艺术一起是对孩子最好的品格教育的理念出发，我们持续举办艺术体验班，特别是针对文化贫困地区加平的孩子们。盖尔美术馆的展览规划为面向家庭的展览，以区别于大型美术馆。盖尔艺术博物馆意味着博物馆参观者的每一天都将是“美好的一天”，是一个配备了多种设施的复合文化空间，包括展示国内外艺术品和举办室内乐、爵士乐等各种表演的艺术厅，以及公众可以直接参与定制音乐会的户外表演厅。

가평 문화 예술 회관은 가평군의 유일한 극장으로서 지역주민의 문화적 욕구.en: Gapyeong Culture and Arts Center is the only theater in Gapyeong-gun and strives to satisfy the cultural needs of local residents. It was completed in 1998 with a total area of ​​4,801 m2, from the 3rd floor underground to the 2nd floor above ground. The main facilities include a large performance hall, multipurpose exhibition hall, outdoor performance hall, projection room, practice room, management office, and electrical and mechanical room. The main performance hall can accommodate 641 seats, and the outdoor performance hall can accommodate 250 people at the same time. You must arrive at the performance hall 20 minutes in advance and enter the audience 10 minutes in advance. Taking photos without prior agreement is prohibited, so be careful when viewing. The remodeling project will be promoted by the end of 2024 as the results of a precise safety diagnosis of the building and stage machinery require repairs.
