It is said to have been founded by Yeongi Josa in 544 (the 22nd year of King Seong of Baekje), and the temple was named after the two letters Hwaeom of the Hwaeom Sutra. At first, only Haehoedang and Daeungsangjeokgwangjeon were built, and then it was expanded by Master Jajang in 643 (the 12th year of the reign of Queen Seondeok), and again in 875 (the first year of King Heongang of Silla) by State Preceptor Doseon. It was destroyed by fire during the Japanese invasions of Korea. In 1630 (the 8th year of King Injo's reign), Master Byeok-Am began to rebuild the temple and completed it 7 years later in the 14th year of King Injo's reign (1636). Inside the temple, there are many cultural heritage sites, including Gakhwangjeon, 4 national treasures, 5 treasures, 1 natural monument, and 2 local cultural heritages, and about 20 annex buildings. In particular, in terms of the layout of the building, if you pass Iljumun Gate and turn about 30 degrees to the northeast, you will reach Cheonwangmun Gate, which houses the statues of Geumgang Station, Munsu, and Bohyeon. This gate has a unique feature in that it is angled towards the west compared to Geumgangmun Gate. If you go up again after passing through the Cheonwangmun Gate, you will reach Bojeru. Bojeru goes around the side of the Nu, which is different from the way to reach the main hall by passing under it from other temples. In that place, dong. The two west towers are visible in a diagonal direction, with Daeungjeon located one step higher than the upper part of the eastern tower, and Gakwangjeon Hall located at the upper part of the western tower. Among the buildings within the precincts, Gakhwangjeon is a very famous building designated as a national treasure. It is the largest existing wooden building in Korea and its magnificent appearance overwhelms the viewer's attention. The stone lantern standing in the front yard of Gakwangjeon is the largest in Korea, with a height of 6.3m and a diameter of 2.8m. It is a work of art that displays the brilliant sculptural art of the Buddhist revival period of the Unified Silla Dynasty and has been designated as National Treasure No. 12. The Four Lions Three-story Stone Pagoda, located on a hill called Hyodae to the left of Gakhwangjeon, was built by the founder of Hwaeomsa Temple to pray for the soul of his mother. It is a masterpiece boasting a unique design and sophisticated carving skills and is a national treasure. The Yeongsanhoe Gwaebultaeng, located at the rear of Gakhwangjeon Hall, was designated as a national treasure in 1997. Among the treasures within the grounds of Hwaeomsa Temple, the five-story pagodas standing on both sides of Daeungjeon are designated as treasures as they are works from the Silla Dynasty that attract attention for their outstanding formativeness and delicate decoration. In addition, the Daeungjeon (treasure) here clearly displays the excellent artistry of the Joseon Dynasty, and with the excellent scenery of Jiri Mountain, a national park, in the background, famous places and scenic spots are scattered here and there. Meanwhile, along National Highway 19 (approximately 35 km) from Hadong to Hwaeomsa Temple, cherry blossom trees are planted as street trees, making it a fantastic driving course every April when the cherry blossoms are in full bloom. Nearby, there are many tourist attractions such as Seomjin River Plum Village, Gosong County Park, Jirisan National Park, and Ssanggyesa Temple, attracting many tourists in spring.

활판공방은 국내에서는 유일하게도 납 활자 인쇄 공정으로 책을 찍어내는 인.en: Letterpress Workshop is the only printing house and publishing company in Korea that prints books using the lead type printing process. The entire process of letterpress printing is almost entirely done by hand in one space, starting from casting, where each letter is made out of lead, to typesetting, where letters are selected from a type shelf filled with approximately 600,000 letters, and typesetting, where the letters are arranged, to printing, folding, and binding. From the entrance, it has a classic atmosphere, with letters and pictures printed on display and books lined up in front. It is said that these are all books printed with letterpress. In addition, machines used for letterpress printing are on display. In addition, we run a separate cafe called Book & Press so that people can easily experience letterpress culture, and we also run experience programs within the workshop.

황산 문화 체육공원은 양산시 물금읍 낙동강변에 대규모로 조성된 공원이다..en: Hwangsan Culture and Sports Park is a large-scale park built along the Nakdong River in Mulgeum-eup, Yangsan-si. It is equipped with a variety of sports facilities, including a camping site, walking trails, bicycle path, square, garden, and three soccer fields, a baseball field, a volleyball court, a basketball court, and a badminton court. In addition, it is a great place to visit with children as it operates a mini train along with a children's playground. On weekends, the campsites are full and there are many riders riding the cool riverside bike path, enjoying the river breeze. It is a healing space in the city center that the whole family can enjoy together.

황학산 수목원은 자연을 아끼고 사랑하는 사람들을 위한 자연과 인간이 교감.en: Hwanghaksan Arboretum is a space where nature and humans can communicate for those who care and love nature. It consists of 14 theme gardens specialized according to the ecology and functions of plants, including a wetland garden, stone garden, mountain fruit garden, mini garden, and jar garden. Efforts are being made to preserve and restore endangered Danyang sagebrush and sycamore, and to provide forest culture and recreational services.

휴휴암은 강원특별자치도 양양군 현남면 바닷가에 자리한 암자다. 일상의 번.en: Huyuam is a hermitage located on the beach in Hyeonnam-myeon, Yangyang-gun, Gangwon-do. It was created with the meaning of letting go of the worries of daily life and resting again and again. Founded by Monk Hongbeop in 1997, this place began as a temple called Myojeokjeon, but became famous as a place for prayer in 1999 when a rock in the shape of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva lying on the beach was discovered. On the beach below Myojeokjeon, there is a wide rock named Yeonhwadae because it resembles a blooming lotus flower. At Yeonhwadae, you can find Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva rock and a turtle-shaped rock, so it is constantly visited by tourists all year round. In addition, strangely shaped rocks such as toe rock, sole rock, and fist rock add to the mystery. Sometimes you can also see schools of dace coming to the beach to feed. In Huyuam, there are Myojeokjeon Hall, Dharani Cave Hall, Avalokitesvara Temple Bell, and Wisdom Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva Statue. The statue of Bodhisattva Wisdom Avalokitesvara on a hill by the sea is another specialty of Huhyuam. The statue of Wisdom Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, flanked by the Dragon King of the East Sea and the Statue of Namsun Dongja, has a beautiful view of the blue East Sea behind it.

경기생활도자미술관 하반기 기획전 《다음 도예: 세대, 탐색, 확장》은 도.en: Gyeonggi Living Ceramic Art Museum’s second half special exhibition “Next Ceramics: Generation, Exploration, Expansion” seeks to highlight the sensibilities and attempts of a new generation that will open the future of ceramics. The exhibition introduces the work of seven artists born in the 1980s and 1990s. They utilize a wide range of elements, from traditional elements such as moon jar formativeness and Buncheong production techniques to modern production methods such as colorful glaze expressions and 3D modeling and casting. Through this, we explore how the horizons of ceramics are expanding. “Daum Ceramics” will go beyond simply introducing the work of the next generation of artists and will be a venue to reveal the infinite possibilities of ceramic art through intergenerational transmission and experimentation. This exhibition is in line with the previously held Seoul Auction × Korea Ceramic Foundation special auction and exhibition project. The experience of experimenting with the multi-layered possibilities of ceramics on two stages, the art museum and the market, through cooperation between the public and private sectors, demonstrated more clearly the role that the foundation pursues as a public platform. Through this exhibition, the Korea Ceramic Foundation provides artists with an opportunity to meet new audiences and visitors with an opportunity to intuitively experience contemporary ceramic art. Under the name of “Daum Ceramics,” we seek to connect generations, expand traditions, and open a new path for ceramics that will lead to the future. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
경기생활도자미술관 하반기 기획전 《다음 도예: 세대, 탐색, 확장》은 도.zh: 京畿生活陶瓷艺术博物馆下半年特别展览“下一代陶瓷：生成、探索、扩展”旨在突出新一代将开启陶瓷未来的感性和尝试。展览介绍了七位80、90年代出生的艺术家的作品。他们运用了广泛的元素，从月瓶造型和粉青制作技术等传统元素，到彩色釉表现和3D建模和铸造等现代制作方法。通过这一点，我们探索陶瓷的视野是如何扩展的。 “道姆陶瓷”将不仅仅是简单地介绍下一代艺术家的作品，还将成为一个通过代际传播和实验来揭示陶瓷艺术的无限可能性的场所。本次展览与此前举办的首尔拍卖×韩国陶瓷财团特别拍卖及展览项目相配合。通过公共和私营部门的合作，在美术馆和市场两个阶段尝试陶瓷的多层次可能性的经验，更清楚地表明了基金会作为公共平台所追求的作用。通过这次展览，韩国陶瓷基金会为艺术家提供了结识新观众和参观者直观体验当代陶瓷艺术的机会。我们以“Daum Ceramics”之名，力求连接世代，弘扬传统，为陶瓷开辟一条通向未来的新道路。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

도시의 성장 신화가 끝난 지금, 우리는 ‘축소’를 새로운 언어로 읽어야.en: Now that the city’s growth story is over, we must read ‘shrinkage’ as a new language. The exhibition proposes an architectural and urban strategy called "reduction-oriented space" in today's urban reality, such as population decline, regional extinction, single-person households, aging, and reorganization of care. Housing is reorganized as the minimum unit that contains both individual independence and community solidarity, distance is reorganized as the range of care, and architecture is reorganized into manageable scale and recyclable resources. ‘Downscaling’ is not decline, but a process of exploring a sustainable scale of life. A city that embraces more relationships and care by reducing costs, 《2025 Busan Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Platform_My Home is Me》 explores the possibility of an ‘appropriate city’. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
도시의 성장 신화가 끝난 지금, 우리는 ‘축소’를 새로운 언어로 읽어야.zh: 既然城市的成长故事已经结束，我们必须将“收缩”视为一种新的语言。展览针对当今人口减少、区域灭绝、单人家庭、老龄化、照料重组等城市现实，提出了一种名为“减量化空间”的建筑与城市策略。住房被重新组织为既包含个人独立性又包含社区团结的最小单位，距离被重新组织为照顾范围，建筑被重新组织为可管理的规模和可回收的资源。 “缩减”并不是衰落，而是探索可持续生活规模的过程。一座通过降低成本拥抱更多关系和关爱的城市，《2025釜山现当代艺术博物馆平台_我的家就是我》探索“合适的城市”的可能性。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

문화예술공공수장고는 2025 야외 전시 프로젝트 《강주현: 연결의 비정형.en: The Culture and Arts Public Storage Center presents the 2025 outdoor exhibition project “Kang Joo-hyun: Atypical Connection.” The public storage facility, which has geographical characteristics where nature and art coexist, has been developing various contents that reflect the region's cultural identity and ecological environment. This project aims to give a new perspective to the surrounding idle space that we pass by in our daily lives, and to interpret and reconstruct the space anew through the introduction of various media. Furthermore, we want to explore how art can expand and evolve within the multi-layered relationship between nature, space, and the audience, rather than staying within a specific framework or boundary. This exhibition, “The Irregularity of Connection,” goes beyond the fixed role of functional space and poses fundamental questions about the sense of place and publicness of storage, and attempts to interpret its meaning in a new way. It is not simply a closed place to store works, but it contains the will to transform it into an ‘open space’ where art, people, senses and thoughts organically communicate. Through this exhibition, the artist reorganizes the existing concept of public storage and suggests that the space itself can become a living artistic field. The artist's perspective sees storage not just as a physical space, but as a dynamic structure where time, relationships, and senses reside and flow. In other words, this place is no longer a place where works of art statically ‘stay’, but is transformed into an open place that is constantly ‘created’ and ‘transformed’ through the participation and perception of the audience. The title of the exhibition, “The Irregularity of Connection,” symbolically connotes the fundamental concept of this exhibition and the artist’s intention. The title reveals the essence of a relationship that cannot be reduced to a fixed framework, set rules, or one-sided semantic system. In other words, it starts from the recognition that the world is not clearly divided and fixed, but is made up of a multifaceted and fluid network of relationships that constantly change and interact. To visually embody this sense of atypical relationship, the artist uses the formative language of ‘circle’ as a key element. The ‘circles’ of various sizes and colors that appear in the work symbolize the unique and independent beings of ‘me’ and ‘others’, respectively. But these circles never remain isolated. By overlapping, touching, overlapping, and connecting with each other, the boundaries become blurred, and individual beings are no longer fixed entities, but become part of an organic relationship that influences each other. The visual structure created in this way is not fixed as a single pattern, but continues to be perceived differently depending on the viewer's position, distance, and direction of gaze and expands into an open form. In particular, the artist focuses on unpredictable and atypical forms that occur ‘between circles’, that is, in the gap between beings. This ‘form in between’ does not simply function as a physical space or boundary, but rather acts as a creative point where new relationships, sensations, and interpretations occur within the gap. This open gap functions as a sensory space where the audience can think and respond, a mediating field where empathy and communication occur, and becomes an important axis that visually embodies the entire exhibition concept. This project also asks fundamental questions about ‘publicness’. Traditionally, publicness has been institutionally understood as a one-sided relationship of provision and acceptance, but this exhibition redefines it as a dynamic relationship that is constantly analyzed and reorganized. This is also an artistic and social proposal that public space in modern society should go beyond its physical function and become a living space that reflects the diversity and interaction of the community. In the end, public storage is reborn as a testing ground for empathy and connection that asks ‘who will we be connected to and how will we be connected?’ The exhibition 《The Irregularity of Connection》 allows us to reflect anew on space, relationships, and the meaning of existence, and shows that art can be a catalyst that connects life and community beyond a simple visual experience. This exhibition is a venue to explore human existence that expands in relationships with others beyond fixed identities and boundaries, and to artistically experiment with the infinite possibilities of the space where such encounters occur. It is also the starting point of a discourse that seeks the future in a multi-layered network connecting nature and humans, past and present, and individuals and communities.
문화예술공공수장고는 2025 야외 전시 프로젝트 《강주현: 연결의 비정형.zh: 文化艺术公共仓储中心推出2025年户外展览项目“姜珠贤：非典型联系”。该公共仓储设施具有自然与艺术共存的地理特征，一直在开发反映该地区文化特征和生态环境的各种内容。本项目旨在为我们日常生活中经过的周围闲置空间提供一个新的视角，并通过各种媒介的引入来重新解读和重构空间。此外，我们希望探索艺术如何在自然、空间和观众之间的多层次关系中扩展和演变，而不是停留在特定的框架或边界内。本次展览“连接的不规则性”超越了功能空间的固定作用，对存储的场所感和公共性提出了基本问题，并试图以新的方式诠释其意义。它不仅仅是一个存放作品的封闭场所，而是包含将其转变为艺术、人、感官和思想有机交流的“开放空间”的意愿。通过这次展览，艺术家重新梳理了现有公共储藏的概念，并暗示空间本身可以成为一个有生命的艺术场域。艺术家的观点不仅将存储视为物理空间，而且将其视为时间、关系和感官驻留和流动的动态结构。换句话说，这里不再是艺术品静态“停留”的场所，而是转变为一个通过观众的参与和感知不断“创造”和“转化”的开放场所。展览的标题“连接的不规则性”象征性地暗示了本次展览的基本概念和艺术家的意图。标题揭示了一种关系的本质，这种关系不能被简化为固定的框架、既定规则或片面的语义系统。换句话说，它始于认识到世界并不是明确划分和固定的，而是由一个多方面、流动的、不断变化和相互作用的关系网络组成。为了在视觉上体现这种非典型关系的感觉，艺术家使用“圆”的造型语言作为关键元素。作品中出现的各种大小和颜色的“圆圈”，分别象征着“我”和“他者”独特而独立的存在。但这些圈子从来都不是孤立的。通过相互重叠、接触、重叠、连接，界限变得模糊，个体的存在不再是固定的实体，而是成为相互影响的有机关系的一部分。以这种方式创建的视觉结构并不是固定为单一图案，而是根据观看者的位置、距离和注视方向不断地被不同地感知，并扩展为开放的形式。艺术家特别关注发生在“圈子之间”，即存在之间的缝隙中的不可预测和非典型的形式。这种“中间的形式”不仅仅起到物理空间或边界的作用，而是充当一个创造性的点，在间隙内产生新的关系、感觉和解释。这个开放的缝隙作为观众思考和反应的感官空间，作为共情和交流发生的中介场，成为视觉上体现整个展览概念的重要轴线。该项目还提出了有关“公共性”的基本问题。传统上，公共性在制度上被理解为一种片面的提供与接受的关系，但本次展览将其重新定义为一种不断分析和重组的动态关系。这也是一种艺术和社会建议，即现代社会的公共空间应超越其物理功能，成为体现社区多样性和互动性的生活空间。最终，公共存储重生为同理心和连接的试验场，它询问“我们将与谁连接，我们将如何连接？”展览《连接的不规则性》让我们重新思考空间、关系和存在的意义，并表明艺术可以成为超越简单视觉体验的连接生活和社区的催化剂。这个展览是一个探索人类存在的场所，人类的存在在与他人的关系中超越了固定的身份和界限，并以艺术方式实验了这种相遇发生的空间的无限可能性。它也是在连接自然与人类、过去与现在、个人与社区的多层网络中寻求未来的话语的起点。

점점 사라지고 있는 학교 앞 문방구 재현을 통해 추억 회상과 당시 생활사.en: Recall memories and introduce the life history of the time by recreating the stationery store in front of the school, which is gradually disappearing. 점점 사라지고 있는 학교 앞 문방구 재현을 통해 추억 회상과 당시 생활사.zh: 通过再现学校前逐渐消失的文具店，回忆记忆，介绍当时的生活史。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

이번 상설전은 대한민국 근현대사의 중요한 장면이자 동아시아 미술의 전환점.en: This permanent exhibition examines the ‘narrative of the times’ drawn by Lee Ungno, focusing on important scenes in the modern and contemporary history of the Republic of Korea and moments that were turning points in East Asian art. Lee Ungno, who survived a period of upheaval from the colonial period and liberation, the Korean War, to modernization and globalization, has not turned away from the questions of the times and has thought about and recorded reality in the language of art. In the early 20th century, Lee Ungno's work took calligraphy and painting as its starting point, and from the mid-20th century, it developed across a variety of media and formats, including abstraction and figuration, painting, sculpture, and ceramics. His art, formed through this process, has established itself as a universal artistic language that can resonate beyond the boundaries of time and region. This exhibition focuses on the period when his artistic trajectory and horizon of thought expanded and transformed in earnest, and is composed of three stages: from the 1910s to before liberation in 1945, after liberation to before moving to France in 1958, and the period of his stay in France. Lee Ungno's works introduced in this exhibition, starting from bamboo paintings expressing his country's desire for independence, to the <Group Statue> series that pondered issues of division, unification, and world peace, show the process by which his art has expanded its style and subject matter amidst the changes of the times. Lee Ungno's world of work crosses the boundaries between Eastern and Western styles, moving toward constant consideration of the relationship between art and society in the field of global contemporary art. Beyond artistic experimentation, he continues to ask questions about human community and peace that transcend ethnicity, ideology, and boundaries, and presents the practical possibilities that modern art can have with society. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
이번 상설전은 대한민국 근현대사의 중요한 장면이자 동아시아 미술의 전환점.zh: 这个常设展览探讨了李应诺绘制的“时代叙事”，重点关注大韩民国近现代历史中的重要场景以及东亚艺术的转折点。经历了从殖民时期到解放时期、朝鲜战争，再到现代化和全球化的动荡时期的李应诺并没有回避时代问题，并用艺术的语言思考和记录现实。 20世纪初，李应诺的创作以书画为起点，20世纪中叶起，跨越抽象与具象、绘画、雕塑、陶瓷等多种媒介和形式发展。在这个过程中形成的他的艺术已经成为一种能够超越时间和地域界限产生共鸣的通用艺术语言。本次展览聚焦他的艺术轨迹和思想视野真正拓展和转变的时期，分为1910年代至1945年解放前、解放后至1958年移居法国前、留法时期三个阶段。本次展览中介绍的李应诺的作品，从表达国家独立愿望的竹子画，到思考分裂、统一、世界和平问题的《群像》系列，展示了他的艺术在时代变迁中拓展风格和题材的过程。李应诺的作品跨越了东西方风格的界限，在全球当代艺术领域不断思考艺术与社会的关系。除了艺术实验之外，他继续超越种族、意识形态和界限，提出有关人类共同体与和平的问题，并呈现现代艺术与社会的实际可能性。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

《신소장품 보고전》은 대구미술관이 2025년 수집한 작품을 시민에게 투명.en: 《New Collection Report Exhibition》 is an exhibition that transparently discloses the works collected by the Daegu Art Museum in 2025 to the public, showcasing 28 works out of a total of 71 works in the collection. The direction of this collection was mainly Daegu's modern art and art of the 1980s. With the opening of a permanent modern art museum through the remodeling of the Daegu Art Museum, a foundation for sharing with citizens was established, and a demand for expansion of works arose accordingly. In addition, along with 《1980-1989 Daegu Art: Summoning of Figures》 held in February 2025, a collection was carried out to build new figurative art of the 1980s at the collection level. In the case of modern art works, Seo Dong-jin's <Factory Scene>, Park Myeong-jo's <Self-Portrait>, and Jeong Jeong-sik's <Hat> are introduced. These are works that complement materials, periods, and formative aspects that were not previously in the collection. The modern works collected this time will enable expansion into future research and exhibitions along with existing collections. In addition, paying attention to the trend of new shapes appearing in Daegu art in the 1980s, the collected works of Kim Il-hwan, Park Yong-jin, Song Gwang-ik, and Lee Guk-bong are introduced. Their works have something in common: building an individual's formative language in different ways based on shape and looking at the reality of the times. Through this, it forms an important point where the new aspect of figurative art shown by Daegu art in the 1980s can be structured within the collection. The works of artists who were introduced through major exhibitions at the museum in 2024-2025 will also be presented again through collection. Along with Kwon Oh-bong's <Untitled> and Lee Ki-chil's <Residence>, Wael Sharki's first commissioned work in Asia, <Love Story>, will be exhibited. In particular, the significant collection of Daegu artists such as Kwak Hoon and Kwon Se-jin goes beyond support of local artists and creates conditions for the organic expansion of contemporary art discourse within the collection. The museum's collection is expanded not only through purchases but also through donations. In 2025, a large number of works were donated by the surviving families of artists Kang Un-seop and Jeong Ji-hwan, and a representative group of works by each artist was established. In addition, works by Kwak Hoon, Baek Rak-jong, Seo Dong-gyun, Song Gwang-ik, Lee Guk-bong, and Sean Scully were donated. Daegu Art Museum will continue to revitalize the meaning of this donation within its collection. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
《신소장품 보고전》은 대구미술관이 2025년 수집한 작품을 시민에게 투명.zh: 《新收藏报告展》是向公众透明公开大邱美术馆2025年收藏作品的展览，展示了大邱美术馆总共71件藏品中的28件作品。此次收藏的方向主要是大邱的现代艺术和20世纪80年代的艺术。通过改建大邱美术馆，开设永久性现代美术馆，建立了与市民共享的基础，相应地也产生了扩大作品的需求。此外，与2025年2月举办的《1980-1989大邱艺术：人物的召唤》一起进行收藏，在收藏层面构建20世纪80年代新的具象艺术。在现代艺术作品方面，介绍了徐东镇的《工厂场景》、朴明祖的《自画像》、郑正植的《帽子》。这些作品补充了以前收藏中没有的材料、时期和形成方面。此次收藏的现代作品将能够与现有收藏一起扩展到未来的研究和展览。此外，还关注20世纪80年代大邱艺术中出现的新造型潮流，介绍了金日焕、朴龙镇、宋光益、李国峰等人的收藏作品。他们的作品有一个共同点：基于形状、审视时代现实，以不同的方式构建个人的形成语言。通过这一点，它形成了一个重要的点，可以在收藏中构建 20 世纪 80 年代大邱艺术所展示的具象艺术的新方面。 2024-2025年通过美术馆重大展览引进的艺术家作品也将通过收藏再次呈现。与权五峰的《无题》和李基七的《住所》一起展出的还有Wael Sharki在亚洲的首次委托作品《爱情故事》。特别是郭勋、权世珍等大邱艺术家的重要收藏，超出了对当地艺术家的支持，也为当代艺术话语在收藏中的有机扩展创造了条件。博物馆的藏品不仅通过购买而且通过捐赠来扩大。 2025年，艺术家姜恩燮和郑智焕的遗属捐赠了大量作品，并建立了每位艺术家的代表作品群。此外，还捐赠了郭勋、白乐钟、徐东均、宋光益、李国峰、肖恩·斯卡利等人的作品。大邱美术馆将继续在其收藏中重振此次捐赠的意义。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

수원시립미술관 소장품전 «블랑 블랙 파노라마»는 흑과 백이라는 두 축을.en: Suwon Museum of Art’s collection exhibition “Blanc Black Panorama” takes as its starting point the two axes of black and white. Looking at the etymology of the French 'blanc' and the English 'black', there is a linguistic view that both words are derived from roots related to light, fire, or combustion. This can also be linked to the interpretation that the Proto-Indo-European word *bʰleg-, meaning ‘to shine’ or ‘to burn’, is presented as the background. This suggests that white and black, light and darkness, are not concepts that are opposed to each other, but are concepts derived from one origin. A series of processes in which it becomes fire, goes through a state of shining white, and then burns out and remains as black ash. Shining and burning, revealing and hiding are not confrontations, but a chain reaction, and can only appear when they presuppose each other. This goes beyond confrontation and touches on the thought of non-two, ‘not two,’ a state revealed in interdependence, and has an attitude that calls for a sense of connection rather than clear boundaries or definitive judgments. Using this etymological background as a clue, the exhibition breaks away from the segmentary view of understanding the world and looks at the reflective attitude of art in a new light. ‘White’ does not mean not burning, but a state that has not yet been scorched, and ‘black’ does not mean extinction, but a trace of light passing. In this way, the two do not deny each other, but reveal their characteristics in the process of forming a relationship. The 20 or so collections introduced in the exhibition embody this attitude in terms of the form and method of the work. The artist focuses on 'how' to express the relationship with the object rather than 'what' of the object, and leaves performative methods such as repetition and overlap, transcription and accumulation, and drawing and emptying on the surface. This method allows seemingly contradictory elements, such as black and white, light and darkness, revelation and remnant, to operate simultaneously, passing through each other rather than being mutually excluded. Now, where darkness and light touch each other, they intersect and form a relationship with the qualities of ‘filling’ and ‘blank’. In this case, ‘panorama’ does not mean a single viewpoint. It refers to the continuous scene created by placing different works side by side, and the sum of subtle differences and spaces that arise when moving between them. In a scene where black and white, light and darkness, filling and emptiness are constantly switching, the exhibition suggests hesitation rather than conclusion, and a method that leaves room for thought instead of conclusion. Now, rather than delivering a clear message, the work is presented as a condition where viewers can stay at their own pace and examine each other as they exist in a relationship. As you walk through the works, I hope you will encounter your own senses and thoughts in a new way, beyond fixed distinctions. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
수원시립미술관 소장품전 «블랑 블랙 파노라마»는 흑과 백이라는 두 축을.zh: 水原市立美术馆的藏品展《白黑全景》以黑白两条轴线为起点。看看法语“blanc”和英语“black”的词源，有一种语言学观点认为这两个词都源自与光、火或燃烧相关的词根。这也可以与原始印欧语单词 *bʰleg- 的解释联系起来，意思是“闪耀”或“燃烧”，被呈现为背景。这表明白与黑、光与暗并不是相互对立的概念，而是同源的概念。它变成火，经过一系列的过程，经历闪亮的白色状态，然后燃烧殆尽，留下黑色的灰烬。闪耀与燃烧、显露与隐藏不是对抗，而是连锁反应，只有在彼此预设的情况下才会出现。这超越了对抗，触及了非二、“非二”的思想，一种在相互依存中揭示的状态，并且有一种态度，要求一种联系感，而不是明确的界限或明确的判断。以此词源背景为线索，展览跳脱了认识世界的片断视角，以新的视角审视艺术的反思态度。 “白”并不是指不燃烧，而是尚未被烧焦的状态，“黑”并不是指熄灭，而是有一丝光的掠过。这样一来，两人并没有互相否定，而是在形成关系的过程中显露出各自的特点。展览中推出的20余件藏品在作品的形式和方法上都体现了这种态度。艺术家关注的是“如何”表达与对象的关系，而不是表达对象的“什么”，而将重复与重叠、转录与堆积、绘画与放空等表演方式留在了表面。这种方式让黑与白、光明与黑暗、启示与残余等看似矛盾的元素同时运作，彼此穿越而不是相互排斥。现在，黑暗与光明相互接触，它们交叉并形成一种“填充”和“空白”的关系。在这种情况下，“全景”并不意味着单一视点。它是指不同作品并排放置所产生的连续场景，以及它们之间移动时产生的微妙差异和空间的总和。在黑与白、明与暗、充与虚不断切换的场景中，展览提出的是犹豫而不是结论，是一种留有思考空间而不是结论的方法。现在，该作品不再传达明确的信息，而是作为一种条件呈现，让观众可以按照自己的节奏，在关系中相互审视。当你浏览这些作品时，我希望你能超越固定的区别，以一种新的方式遇到自己的感觉和想法。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220

2026 어린이미술기획전 《열한번째 트윙클》은 아이들이 매일 경험하지만.en: The 2026 Children’s Art Exhibition “Eleventh Twinkle” is an exhibition that helps children understand the ‘state of mind’ that they experience every day but cannot easily express in words through changes in form. We focus on the fact that emotions are not fixed properties, but structural events whose volume, texture, density, and slope vary depending on the situation and relationship. Author Seungwon Jeong unfolds the subtle emotions and moments found in everyday scenes with fairytale colors and characters, transforming familiar scenes into ‘stories that linger in the heart.’ His work visualizes small emotions such as joy, awkwardness, excitement, and disappointment that seep into a child's heart through color temperature, facial expressions, and movement, and serves as the narrative background for the “11 sparkles,” or Twinkle, that the exhibition refers to. Artist Baek In-kyo has applied changes in elasticity, gravity, and pressure to threads, fibers, and everyday objects, expanding his work into formative experiments that allow the body to experience the process of shapes being pushed, shaken, and returned. In Baekin-gyo's installation work, children directly see, touch, move, and experience changes in their hearts, such as broadening or narrowing, hardening and then loosening, and rounding or sharpening. The exhibition is not designed as a space to correct or evaluate emotions, but as a small laboratory in which children develop the ability to understand and express their own emotional structure. During the day, children create a ‘heart shape’ that corresponds to their emotions, and visually learn how the mind changes through a combination of lines, planes, colors, and densities. The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220
2026 어린이미술기획전 《열한번째 트윙클》은 아이들이 매일 경험하지만.zh: 2026年儿童艺术展“第十一闪”是一个通过形式的变化，让孩子们了解自己每天所经历却无法轻易用言语表达的“心境”的展览。我们关注这样一个事实：情绪不是固定的属性，而是结构事件，其体积、纹理、密度和斜率根据情况和关系而变化。作者郑承源以童话般的色彩和人物展现日常生活场景中的微妙情感和时刻，将熟悉的场景转化为“萦绕在心间的故事”。他的作品通过色温、面部表情和动作将渗入孩子内心的喜悦、尴尬、兴奋、失望等小情绪形象化，并作为展览所指的“11个闪光”或“闪烁”的叙事背景。艺术家白仁教将弹性、重力和压力的变化应用于线、纤维和日常物品，将他的作品扩展到形成性实验，让身体体验形状被推动、震动和返回的过程。在白金桥的装置作品中，孩子们直接看到、触摸、移动，体验着内心的变化，比如变宽或变窄、变硬或变松、变圆或变尖。展览的目的不是作为一个纠正或评估情绪的空间，而是作为一个小实验室，孩子们可以在其中培养理解和表达自己情绪结构的能力。白天，孩子们会创造出与他们的情绪相对应的“心形”，并通过线条、平面、颜色和密度的组合直观地了解思想如何变化。演出/展览节目可能会根据主办方、表演者等情况而改变。 1688-2220
